tables44.title: The 44 tables this migration creates
tables44.note: 41 tables for the data products, plus sys_objects and sys_fields which hold the data dictionary, plus data_product which is the catalog of the 14 products.

items.c: Account collateral: Which collateral secures which account.
Account payment: A payment posted to a loan account.
Asset: An asset the bank holds after repossession, deed in lieu or auction purchase.
Asset sale: The sale of an asset.
Assignment: Who holds a case or a task and from when.
Case account: Links each loan account to the case it is recovered under.
Case party: The role each party plays on a case.
Collateral: Property or vehicle securing one or more accounts.
Contact point: A way to reach a party, with its consent and whether it works.
Data product: One of the 14 data products, with its single system of record, owner and refresh cycle.
Debt sale account: An account in a debt sale lot.
Debt sale lot: A lot of accounts offered to debt buyers.
Decision log entry: One record per decision. Append only and hash chained.
Delegation limit: An approval limit by decision, level, product and amount.
Deviation: A deviation X1 to X7 raised on a case.
Document: A document held against a case.
Document custody: Each movement of an original document.
Document field: A field read from a document.
Guarantee claim: A claim against a Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation guarantee or an insurer.
Hearing: A court hearing on a legal action.
Interaction: One entry in the interaction ledger: a contact, letter, promise, payment or hand-over.
Legal action: A notice, lawsuit, appeal, enforcement or bankruptcy action on a case.
Listing: An asset offered for sale, with its prices and rounds.
Loan account: A loan account in the core bank.
List value: A value in a list of values.
Notice: A demand, recall or statutory notice and its proof of delivery.
Partner: An outside firm the bank places work with.
Partner instruction: Work placed with a partner on a case.
Party: A person or company with a role on one or more cases.
Permission: What a role may do in one capability area.
Proceeds: Money received on a case and what it was matched to.
Queue: A queue of work belonging to one team and one role.
Recovery case: One recovery case per customer per product, from 90 days past due to close.
Role: A Workbench role, held as data.
Rule: One versioned routing rule or sentry.
Score: A score or estimate COLLINS returns for an account or case.
Sys fields: The metadata registry of fields: the data dictionary held as data.
Sys objects: The metadata registry of entities: one row per object in the data dictionary.
Task: A unit of work on a case: a CMMN human, customer, partner or decision task.
Template: A letter or notice template.
Timer: A running clock on a case: a service level, a legal period or an offer validity.
Treatment: A resolution put to the customer or carried out on the case, with its terms and outcome.
Valuation: An appraisal of collateral or an asset.
Write-off: A write-off of the balance on a case.

fields410.title: The 410 fields
fields410.note: 108 arrive from a source system and 302 are created in the Workbench. They are listed in Source to Target Mapping v3.

objects41.title: The 41 entities in the data dictionary
objects41.note: One sys_objects row each. The three metadata and catalog tables do not describe themselves.

items.c: Account collateral: Which collateral secures which account.
Account payment: A payment posted to a loan account.
Asset: An asset the bank holds after repossession, deed in lieu or auction purchase.
Asset sale: The sale of an asset.
Assignment: Who holds a case or a task and from when.
Case account: Links each loan account to the case it is recovered under.
Case party: The role each party plays on a case.
Collateral: Property or vehicle securing one or more accounts.
Contact point: A way to reach a party, with its consent and whether it works.
Debt sale account: An account in a debt sale lot.
Debt sale lot: A lot of accounts offered to debt buyers.
Decision log entry: One record per decision. Append only and hash chained.
Delegation limit: An approval limit by decision, level, product and amount.
Deviation: A deviation X1 to X7 raised on a case.
Document: A document held against a case.
Document custody: Each movement of an original document.
Document field: A field read from a document.
Guarantee claim: A claim against a Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation guarantee or an insurer.
Hearing: A court hearing on a legal action.
Interaction: One entry in the interaction ledger: a contact, letter, promise, payment or hand-over.
Legal action: A notice, lawsuit, appeal, enforcement or bankruptcy action on a case.
Listing: An asset offered for sale, with its prices and rounds.
Loan account: A loan account in the core bank.
List value: A value in a list of values.
Notice: A demand, recall or statutory notice and its proof of delivery.
Partner: An outside firm the bank places work with.
Partner instruction: Work placed with a partner on a case.
Party: A person or company with a role on one or more cases.
Permission: What a role may do in one capability area.
Proceeds: Money received on a case and what it was matched to.
Queue: A queue of work belonging to one team and one role.
Recovery case: One recovery case per customer per product, from 90 days past due to close.
Role: A Workbench role, held as data.
Rule: One versioned routing rule or sentry.
Score: A score or estimate COLLINS returns for an account or case.
Task: A unit of work on a case: a CMMN human, customer, partner or decision task.
Template: A letter or notice template.
Timer: A running clock on a case: a service level, a legal period or an offer validity.
Treatment: A resolution put to the customer or carried out on the case, with its terms and outcome.
Valuation: An appraisal of collateral or an asset.
Write-off: A write-off of the balance on a case.

confirmed_by.c: Who confirmed a low confidence value

extracted_value.c: The value as first read by the extractor, kept when a person corrects field_value; masked by role

extractor_version.c: Extraction approach and model version that produced the value

from_location.c: Vault, branch, post, lawyer, court, land office

decision_code.c: D5.1 to D9.3, X1 to X7, or an access event

inputs_ref.c: Reference to the inputs snapshot, with the freshness of each input

override_reason.c: Reason when the person did not follow the recommendation

actions.c: Target system, result and timestamps of each action

chain_seq.c: Position of the entry in the hash chain; prev_hash is the entry_hash of chain_seq minus 1; unique on its own

actor_user_id.c: The person or service identity whose action, preparation or access the entry records

model_code.c: Model, for example CRR_RET_380 asset pricing

estimate_value.c: Estimated amount, baht, for example return by route or sale price

account_payment_id.c: The account_payment this record belongs to

matched_to.c: Installment, settlement, fee, sale proceeds, unmatched

posting_ref.c: Posting reference in the core or GL

tax_criteria_met.c: True when the tax criteria are met

recovered_after.c: Recovered after charge-off to date, baht

test_case_id.c: Test case that proves the rule

rule_table.c: The Epic 1 rule table a row belongs to

row_order.c: Order in which rows of one rule table are evaluated; first match wins

target_queue_code.c: The queue an allocation or transfer row places the case in

principal_limit.c: Principal limit, baht; empty means no limit

min_price_pct_fmv.c: Lowest sale price as a percentage of fair market value

substitute_user_id.c: Substitute when the holder is absent

limit_version.c: Delegation version the row belongs to, for example DOA-2026.11

regulation_item.c: Item of Regulation กกค.540031, for example 2.1.1; one decision code covers several items

applies_when.c: Case condition that selects the row, WO_CRITERIA_MET or WO_CRITERIA_NOT_MET for item 2.1.10

max_loss_amount.c: Maximum loss the level may approve, baht

max_delay_count.c: Most delays of legal action, seizure or auction the level may approve on a case

min_price_pct_principal.c: Lowest sale price as a percentage of principal outstanding

min_received_pct.c: Lowest amount received against the total debt, percent

max_term_years.c: Longest lease term the level may approve, years

role_class.c: Bank user, partner user, non-human actor

entra_group.c: Entra ID group mapped to the role

role_id.c: The role this record belongs to

letters.c: C, R, U, D and A, or a dash for none

template_version.c: Version; unique with template_code, since a template holds several versions

approved_by_legal.c: True once Legal approves the wording

signature_basis.c: How Legal allows the document to be signed

merge_codes.c: The merge codes the template body uses

product_name.c: Data product name, for example Account and arrears

system_of_record.c: The one system of record for the product

refresh_cycle.c: Daily, weekly, monthly or on change

expected_by.c: Time the load is expected by, for example 08:00 or MON 08:00

can_read.c: True when the role may read the product

access_version.c: Version of the access table, for example DPA-2026.11

source_extracted_at.c: When the source extract was taken, from the COLLINS control record or the file

loaded_at.c: When the load committed in the Workbench

stale_flagged_at.c: When the product was flagged stale

duplicate_count.c: Repeat stamps ignored for the same product and business date

contract_code.c: Contract code per source system, for example DC-ALS

interface_id.c: Interfaces covered, for example INT-01, INT-02

confirmed_by_role.c: Role of the system owner who confirmed, for example ALS system owner

confirmation_document_ref.c: Stored confirmation from the system owner

field_id.c: BR Field ID, for example DF-CAS-001

data_type.c: TSD data type: TEXT, NUMBER, DATE, BOOLEAN, LOV, USER_REF, CROSS_REF, FORMULA or ATTACHMENT

is_mandatory.c: True when the field is required

references_object.c: Table a cross-reference field points to

source_field.c: Field name in the source system

is_personal.c: True for personal data under PDPA

late_behavior.c: What the Workbench does when the value is missing or late

job_code.c: Job the run belongs to, for example JOB-01

rows_held.c: Records held in the exception list

failed_check.c: Check that refused the load, for example DQ-003

check_results.c: Result per check code, plus the sample and other counts

interface_run_id.c: The P2 interface run the file load belongs to

load_run_id.c: The load run that raised it

check_code.c: Load check (DQ-nnn), row rule (DQnn), reconciliation (REC-nn) or tracker check (TRK-nn)

record_key.c: Business key of the failing record, for example the account number; never personal data

reason_code.c: Reason code shown to the data product owner

rule_type.c: Not null, unique across, range, sum equals, exists link, maximum age in days, field before

rule_params.c: Fields and values for the rule type

transformation.c: Transformation type and parameters: COPY_TRIM, SUM, TO_DATE_BE, TO_NUMERIC_2, BOOLEAN_YN, CODE_MAP, BUSINESS_DATE

approval_ref.c: Reference of the system owner's sign-off on the mapping version

location_type.c: Excel, SharePoint, local file or none

field_list.c: Field names with the personal data tag and the optional mapped-to field

update_cycle.c: Daily, weekly, monthly or ad hoc

target_product.c: Target data product for a LOAD decision

last_load_run_id.c: Latest load run of the tracker

signed_off_by.c: Team manager who signed off the load

source_file_ref.c: Stored tracker file in the write-once store

archive_ref.c: Read-only archive location of the retired tracker

retire_confirmed_by.c: Team manager who confirmed the retirement

unfed_fields.c: Non-personal tracker fields no data product field carries

field_values.c: Non-personal tracker fields of the row

last_contact_at.c: Latest EFS contact across the case's accounts

last_action_code.c: Action code of the latest contact

publish_status.c: Pending, held or released for the date's extract

copy_name.c: Name of the copy; DECISION_LOG for the decision log lake copy

last_entry_hash.c: Entry hash of the last decision log entry copied and matched

last_decided_at.c: decided_at of the last entry copied

rows_copied_total.c: Cumulative count of entries in the lake copy

table_name.c: Table the rule applies to, from sys_objects; never decision_log_entry

record_class.c: Retention class from LOV-RETENTION, or LAKE_COPY for the decision log lake copy

age_basis_field.c: Field the age is measured from, for example interaction.occurred_at

end_action.c: Archive or review at the end of the period

reference_version_id.c: Reference version that brought the row

guarantee_claim_id.c: The guarantee claim copied; unique with business_date

file_pattern.c: File name pattern with the business date

max_attempts.c: Most send attempts before the exception queue

retry_intervals_min.c: Minutes between attempts, comma separated, for example 5,15,45

alert_role.c: Role alerted on a refused or missing file

checks.c: Result of each check and the run summary counts

clean_days.c: Clean days in a row at sign-off

case_ids.c: Cases whose step waits on the file

next_attempt_at.c: When the next attempt is due

last_error.c: Last transfer error, no personal data

event_id.c: Outbox event of the first delivery, where the key came from an event

endpoint.c: Method and path of the request

response.c: Stored response returned to a repeat

event_type.c: Event name from EV-01 to EV-28, or an outbound work request type such as WIN_DISPATCH

schema_version.c: Schema version of the payload; consumers accept the current and previous version

payload.c: References and codes only; no personal data

last_error_code.c: Code of the last failure returned by the consumer

removal_date.c: Date by which the flag and its old path are removed

job_name.c: Job name from the batch schedule

schedule_text.c: Schedule as in the batch schedule

runbook_path.c: Path of the run book in the repository

alert_after_minutes.c: Duration after which the owner is alerted

first_release.c: Epic of first release, for example E1

product_type.c: Product type from the customer profile

product_status.c: Active, delinquent, closed or written off

in_ledger.c: True when rows with this action code enter the ledger

capacity.c: Most open cases the person may hold in the queue

skill_codes.c: Skills of the person, comma separated

avg_age_days.c: Average age of the open cases, days

max_age_days.c: Age of the oldest open case, days

owner_min.c: Fewest open cases held by one owner

owner_max.c: Most open cases held by one owner

breached.c: Open cases past their service level

kind.c: Kind of parameter, for example ENVIRONMENT for an environment setting

unit.c: Unit, for example CALENDAR_DAYS, WORKING_DAYS, BAHT, PERCENT, COUNT, CODE_LIST

scope.c: Product, when the parameter is keyed by product group, or global

required.c: True when every product in force must have a row

environments.c: Environments the parameter is set in

used_by.c: Modules and stories that read the parameter

secret.c: True for a secret; its value is never returned

table_code.c: The reference or rule table the version belongs to, for example EXPOSURE_BAND or ALLOCATION

version_label.c: Version label the rows carry, for example DOCTYPE-2026.11

content_hash.c: SHA-256 of the rows sorted by key; used for idempotency

load_id.c: Identifier of the reference load request that created the version

dry_run_counts.c: Counts of live cases each changed rule row would move, from the dry run

change_request_ref.c: Reference of the change request in the bank's request tool

impact_summary.c: What the change affects, for example the open cases it touches

test_result.c: Passed or failed, from the load checks or the rule table test harness

rollback_plan.c: How to return to the previous version

verified_by.c: Who verified the change after it took effect

version_id.c: The reference version the row belongs to; unique with row_key

row_key.c: Key of the row inside its table

facts.c: Synthetic case file facts the condition reads

result_detail.c: Expected against actual, and the rows that hit

unmasked.c: True when the role sees the field unmasked; no row means masked

masking_version.c: Version of the masking rules, for example MASK-2026.11

conflicts_with.c: Role code, or ANY_BUSINESS_ROLE or ANY_OTHER_ROLE, per the Separation of duty sheet

conflict_version.c: Version of the conflict table, for example SOD-2026.11

doc_type_code.c: Document type code, the value set of LOV-DOC-TYPE

field_definitions.c: Fields extracted from the type: name, label, data type, personal flag, required flag, extraction method (TEMPLATE or MODEL), review only flag and optional pattern

legal_signoff_by.c: Legal counsel user who signed the type and its fields

npa_signoff_by.c: Head of NPA user who signed the type and its fields

classify_threshold.c: Confidence below which a document of this type goes to the review queue

complete.c: True when every required type is present; empty when the stage has no checklist

last_event_id.c: Event that triggered the last check, for repeat detection

param_code.c: Parameter code, for example INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB, OCR_MIN_QUALITY, CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD, CASE_NO_PATTERN, SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS

channel_code.c: Branch code, MAILROOM, partner code or mailbox code

sender_address.c: Sender email address for mailbox items; masked by role

run_id.c: JOB-12 run that took the item in

received_at.c: When the Workbench received the file

intake_ref.c: Received file in the intake container

scan_result.c: Malware scan result: clean or infected; empty until scanned

ocr_ref.c: OCR JSON output (text and layout) in the standard container

ocr_attempts.c: Number of OCR calls made for the item

rescan_pages.c: Page numbers below the OCR quality threshold

ocr_quality.c: Lowest page quality of the item

ocr_engine_version.c: Version of the OCR service that read the item

predicted_type.c: Type with the highest classification score

type_candidates.c: Top two types with their scores

classifier_version.c: Model version that classified the item

classify_fallback.c: True when the classifier did not answer and the item went to a person

match_status.c: Pending, matched, no match, multiple, conflict, case closed or no type

candidate_case_ids.c: Cases found for the item when more than one or none can be chosen by rule

extracted_fields.c: Fields read before the item is attached: field name, value, extracted value, confidence, state, extractor version, personal flag

review_reason.c: Why the item needs a person: rescan, unreadable file, low confidence, model unavailable, unknown type

review_outcome.c: Attached or discarded once a person resolves the review item

resolved_at.c: When the review item was resolved

discard_reason.c: Reason given when a review item is discarded

intake_id.c: Intake item the page belongs to; unique with page_no

text_content.c: OCR text of the page; masked by role on read

quality.c: Mean word confidence of the page

run_month.c: Month of the JOB-17 run, YYYY-MM

merge_code.c: Code written in the template body, for example CASE_NO

is_required.c: True when generation holds on an empty value

personal_data.c: True when the value is personal data, detokenized only at generation

route_role_code.c: Role for a decision with no amount limit, for example RW-LITOFF

delegation_limit_id.c: Delegation row that covers the item

prepared_by.c: Person or service identity that prepared the item

assigned_user_id.c: Holder the item is assigned to; empty for a role route

source_type.c: What asked for approval, for example NOTICE or TREATMENT

amount_tolerance_pct.c: Allowed difference from the installment, 0 to 100 percent

window_days_before.c: Days before the due date a payment may arrive

window_days_after.c: Days after the due date a payment may arrive

grace_days.c: Days after the due date before PaymentMissed is raised

partial_floor_pct.c: Lowest share of the installment matched as partial, percent

priority.c: Order in which rows are tried

dimension_code.c: Dimension: route, age band, queue, stage or agent

is_baseline.c: True for a row of the baseline date

frozen.c: True when the row may not change

case_list_count.c: Open cases on the case list at the cut-off

dashboard_count.c: Open cases in the dashboard facts

agent_code.c: Agent or model, for example INTAKE, SCREENING, LEGAL_DOC, EXTRACT, TDR_OFFER

output_schema_ref.c: Reference to the JSON Schema the answer must meet

allowed_tools.c: Tools the agent may call through the tool gateway

segment_product_group.c: Product group the mode applies to; empty for all

segment_region_code.c: Region the mode applies to; empty for all

confidence_floor.c: Answers below this confidence fall back or are marked for review

timeout_seconds.c: Seconds the gateway waits before the rule result is used

daily_cost_cap_thb.c: Daily model cost limit per agent, baht

review_date.c: Date the version is reviewed again, for a parked or shadow agent

evaluation_run_id.c: Evaluation run an autonomy step is based on

promotion_conditions.c: Conditions the evaluation must meet for the stated mode

watch_measures.c: Measures and limits to watch after the step, including drift points and minimum feedback

fallback_rule.c: Rule applied when the agent does not answer, for example R-UNI-32

body_text.c: Prompt text with placeholders; no personal data

subject_id.c: Document, legal action or treatment the run is about, where not the case

fallback.c: True when the rule result was used instead of the answer

output.c: Checked answer, masked; never returned for shadow runs

latency_ms.c: Time from call to answer or timeout, milliseconds

tokens_in.c: Input tokens returned by the endpoint

tokens_out.c: Output tokens returned by the endpoint

label_key.c: Gap type, deviation code, field name or checklist item

expected_value.c: Labeled value; SHA-256 hash for personal values

total_cost_thb.c: Cost of all runs in the evaluation, baht

failure_counts.c: Count of runs by failure status and check code

proposal.c: Proposed approach and confidence threshold per document type

review_count.c: Proposals below the confidence floor, scored separately

approach.c: Agent, OCR template, model, or OCR and model

agreement_rate.c: Share of subjects where the answer equals the label

agent_run_id.c: Agent run the feedback is on

item_key.c: SUMMARY for the intake summary, or the deviation code

measured_value.c: Cost in baht or acceptance rate measured

threshold_value.c: Limit the value was compared with

entity.c: The table the field belongs to

migration.en: A numbered SQL file that changes the database. The tool applies each file once, in order, and keeps a record of which ones it has run, so every environment ends up the same.
migration.th: ไฟล์ SQL ที่มีหมายเลขกำกับ ใช้เปลี่ยนโครงสร้างฐานข้อมูล ระบบจะรันแต่ละไฟล์เพียงครั้งเดียวตามลำดับ

Flyway.en: The tool that applies the migration files and records which have run, in a table of its own.
Flyway.th: เครื่องมือที่รันไฟล์ migration และบันทึกว่ารันไฟล์ใดไปแล้ว

schema.en: A named container inside the database that holds tables. The Workbench uses one called recovery.
schema.th: พื้นที่ในฐานข้อมูลที่ใช้เก็บตาราง

foreign key.en: A rule that says a value in one table must exist in another. It stops a row pointing at something that is not there, such as a case on an account that does not exist.
foreign key.th: กฎที่บังคับว่าค่าของตารางหนึ่งต้องมีอยู่จริงในอีกตารางหนึ่ง

index.en: A lookup structure the database keeps so it can find rows quickly without reading the whole table.
index.th: โครงสร้างที่ช่วยให้ฐานข้อมูลค้นหาแถวได้เร็วขึ้น

trigger.en: A piece of code the database runs by itself whenever a row is inserted, changed or deleted.
trigger.th: โค้ดที่ฐานข้อมูลรันเองเมื่อมีการเพิ่ม แก้ไข หรือลบข้อมูล

append-only.en: Rows can be added but never changed or deleted. A correction is a new row, so the earlier record stays readable.
append-only.th: เพิ่มข้อมูลได้อย่างเดียว แก้ไขหรือลบไม่ได้ การแก้ไขทำโดยเพิ่มแถวใหม่

transaction.en: A group of changes that either all succeed or all fail. Nothing half-finished is left behind.
transaction.th: กลุ่มของการเปลี่ยนแปลงที่ต้องสำเร็จทั้งหมดหรือไม่สำเร็จเลย

view.en: A saved query that behaves like a table when you read from it.
view.th: คำสั่งค้นหาที่บันทึกไว้ และเรียกใช้ได้เหมือนตาราง

seed rows.en: The first rows a migration puts into a table so the system has something to work with.
seed rows.th: ข้อมูลตั้งต้นที่ migration ใส่ลงตารางตั้งแต่แรก

conformance test.en: An automated check in the build that compares the real database against the data dictionary, both ways, and fails the build if they disagree.
conformance test.th: การตรวจสอบอัตโนมัติที่เทียบฐานข้อมูลจริงกับพจนานุกรมข้อมูล

idempotent.en: Running it a second time changes nothing more. The result after two runs is the same as after one.
idempotent.th: ทำซ้ำแล้วผลลัพธ์เหมือนเดิม ไม่เปลี่ยนแปลงเพิ่ม

endpoint.en: A web address the Workbench exposes that another system or a screen can call.
endpoint.th: ที่อยู่ที่ระบบอื่นเรียกใช้งานได้

handler.en: A class that implements one named job. Reference data loads pick the handler by table code.
handler.th: คลาสที่ทำหน้าที่เฉพาะอย่างหนึ่ง

parameter.en: A setting held outside the code and set per environment, so the same build runs in DEV and SIT.
parameter.th: ค่าที่ตั้งไว้นอกโค้ด และกำหนดแยกตามสภาพแวดล้อม

data dictionary.en: The list of every field, its type, its source and its owner, held as data in the database rather than in a document.
data dictionary.th: รายการของทุกฟิลด์ ชนิดข้อมูล แหล่งที่มา และผู้รับผิดชอบ

system of record.en: The one system whose value is the true one when systems disagree.
system of record.th: ระบบต้นทางหลักที่ถือว่าข้อมูลถูกต้องที่สุด

DEV.en: The development environment. The first place a change runs.
DEV.th: สภาพแวดล้อมสำหรับพัฒนา

SIT.en: System integration test. The environment where the parts are tested together.
SIT.th: สภาพแวดล้อมสำหรับทดสอบการเชื่อมต่อระบบ

primary key.en: The column whose value identifies a row and never repeats in that table.
primary key.th: คอลัมน์ที่ใช้ระบุแถว และห้ามซ้ำ

unique constraint.en: A rule that stops the same value appearing twice in a column.
unique constraint.th: กฎที่ห้ามค่าซ้ำในคอลัมน์

Pipeline.who: The build and deployment chain. It runs on its own when code is merged, applies the migrations and runs the tests. A developer does not run these steps by hand; they write what the pipeline runs.
Pipeline.th: ระบบอัตโนมัติ ไม่มีคนทำ

Migration.who: The SQL file itself, while it is being applied. A step that starts with Migration describes what that file does to the database.
Migration.th: ไฟล์ SQL ขณะกำลังทำงาน

System.who: The Workbench application, acting without anyone pressing anything.
System.th: ระบบทำงานเอง

Developer.who: A TechX engineer building the story.

Data steward.who: The person accountable for a data product, who confirms its catalog entry.
Data steward.th: ผู้ดูแลข้อมูล

Reference data administrator.who: The person who loads reference data files, such as the data product catalog, through the admin screens.
Reference data administrator.th: ผู้ดูแลข้อมูลอ้างอิง

Platform administrator.who: The person who sets environment parameters and operates the platform.
Platform administrator.th: ผู้ดูแลแพลตฟอร์ม

Case owner.who: The officer who holds the case.
Case owner.th: เจ้าของกรณี

Team manager.who: The manager of a collections or recovery team.
Team manager.th: ผู้จัดการทีม

open.q: Is access to the Workbench granted centrally or by the application owner?
open.opts:
A: a central IAM or IT security team grants and reviews access.
B: application owner administration. Role owners approve each grant and an access administrator in the business carries it out.
open.rec: B. SCB IT administers business applications this way today, and the Workbench build is the same under both options.
open.blocks: Users, roles and permissions; role to system access matrix; security and access design; administration stories
open.late: The access tests for the Epic 1 release have no named signers.

open.q: Who owns the Workbench as an application?
open.opts:
A: the Tribe Lead of the Collections and Recovery Tribe, for ACE as a whole, with recovery roles delegated to recovery role owners.
B: a separate owner for the recovery module.
C: the ACE team in SCB Data and AI.
open.rec: A, with the ACE team as technical custodian. ACE holds the collection and recovery modules in one service.
open.blocks: Admin and access model; users, roles and permissions; run operating model
open.late: No one can approve a role, appoint role owners or sign the access review.

open.q: Who makes the architecture change that lets partners reach the Workbench from outside the bank, given a lead time of one to three months?
open.opts:
A: the Workbench team raises the change with the architecture team now.
B: the ACE team raises it as part of making ACE internet facing.
C: partners stay on their existing channels until after Epic 8.
open.rec: A or B, raised in November. Law firms are first needed at Epic 5, litigation, in March 2027.
open.owner: K. Book with the architecture team
open.blocks: Security and access design; non-functional specification; partner operating model
open.late: A request after November leaves law firms outside the Workbench at the litigation release.

open.q: Who merges code between the recovery and collection squads, and who decides when one squad's change holds the release?
open.opts:
A: each squad merges into its own module through code owners; the ACE team owns the common module and the release decision.
B: one release manager in the ACE team merges all changes.
C: the merge role rotates between squads.
open.rec: A. A change that fails SIT or UAT is switched off by its feature flag and the release goes ahead.
open.blocks: Engineering practices; environment and deployment design
open.late: Two squads commit to one service from 2 November with no agreed merge owner.

open.q: Does the bank create the Workbench module in ACE, or does TechX?
open.opts:
A: the ACE team creates the module folders and the boundary checks.
B: TechX creates the recovery module in its own package now, and the ACE team applies the module boundaries as it moves ACE to the modular monolith.
open.rec: B from 2 November, then A.
open.blocks: Engineering practices; technical enabler stories
open.late: TechX has no agreed place to commit code on 2 November.

open.q: Which interfaces need real time data, and which take the daily batch?
open.opts:
A: daily batch through COLLINS for all Epic 1 and Epic 2 data, with events added later for named same-day triggers.
B: real time APIs now for a named list of interfaces.
open.rec: A. ACE has no real time feed today. Name the same-day triggers now: case transferred from EFS, payment received, legal event.
open.blocks: Information flow; integration inventory; interface specifications
open.late: Interface specifications are written against an unknown data freshness.

open.q: How is the ACE front end split into modules?
open.opts:
A: one ACE front end with a recovery module folder.
B: one ACE front end split into a workspace of modules with NX.
C: a separate front end for recovery.
open.rec: A from 2 November. The NX split is the ACE team's choice and does not hold the build.
open.blocks: Environment and deployment design; design system; screen specifications
open.late: Screens built in November may need to move between folders.

RWB-E1-001.1: Create one Flyway migration file at src/main/resources/db/migration/recovery/V1_001__recovery_schema.sql. Its contents come from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql, which holds the DDL for all 108 tables of the recovery module. This story needs 44 of them. Wherever that file fixes the schema name, put the placeholder ${recoverySchema} instead, which Flyway fills in when it runs. Add recoverySchema to the configuration service with the value recovery for both DEV and SIT. You never run the file by hand. Merging your branch is what makes the pipeline apply it, so the file has to be correct before it is merged.
RWB-E1-001.2: Create all 44 tables inside one transaction, so a failure part way through leaves the schema untouched. Copy the columns, primary keys and unique constraints from Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v4.sql without changing a name or a type, because the test in step 4 compares them against the dictionary and fails on any difference. Declare the foreign keys as ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT statements after the tables exist, which is the form the schema file uses. Add the two triggers that call refuse_change() on decision_log_entry and interaction, so neither table accepts an UPDATE or a DELETE. Reconcile the counts first: this step says 68 foreign keys and 76 indexes, and the schema file now holds 66 and 76 for these tables.
RWB-E1-001.3: Insert the dictionary rows in the same migration. One row in sys_objects for each of the 41 entities, and one row in sys_fields for each field of those tables, with the values taken from Recovery Workbench Source to Target Mapping v3.xlsx, which lists every field with its entity, data product, physical type, source system and source field. Insert the 14 data_product rows before the sys_objects rows, because sys_objects.data_product has a foreign key to data_product.product_code. Leave owner_user_id empty; a person supplies it in step 6. Then create the view v_data_dictionary, joining sys_objects, sys_fields and data_product so one query returns everything about a field. The schema file has no definition for that view, so you write it.
RWB-E1-001.4: Write the conformance test as a pipeline test, not a unit test, because it has to run against a real database after the migration. Read the live columns from information_schema.columns for the recovery schema, read the rows of sys_fields, and compare in both directions. Fail the build if a real column has no dictionary row, if a dictionary row has no column, or if the physical types differ. Leave the 7 standard columns out of the comparison. The failure message must name the column that caused it, because AC5 asserts the exact wording.
RWB-E1-001.5: No new code. The pipeline promotes the same artifact to SIT and runs the migration and the test again there. Flyway keeps its own table of which versions it has applied, so a second run finds 1.001 already applied and does nothing, which is what AC6 checks by comparing the row counts of sys_objects and sys_fields before and after.
RWB-E1-001.6: Build the load path for this table code. The reference data administrator sends the catalog file to POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads with the table code data_product, a validFrom date and the multipart file. Implement the endpoint if RWB-E1-043 has not already delivered it, and implement DataProductCatalogHandler as the ReferenceTableHandler registered for that code, which is how a load finds the class that handles it. The file holds the 14 products with the owner user ID for that environment, so DEV and SIT are given different files.
RWB-E1-001.7: Implement validate on DataProductCatalogHandler. Refuse the file unless it holds exactly DP01 to DP14 with none missing and none repeated, and unless every row names exactly one system of record, one owner role that exists in LOV-ROLE, one owner user ID, and one refresh cycle from DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY and ON_CHANGE. Return MSG-P1-003, MSG-P1-004 and MSG-P1-007 for the cases AC7, AC8 and AC9 set out. Validation writes nothing at all: one bad row refuses the whole file.
RWB-E1-001.8: Do not apply the load when it is uploaded. A second person has to approve it first, so the load stays pending until the data steward who owns the catalog approves it through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve with Reference data A. Record both the load and the approval in the decision log. This is what stops one person changing reference data alone.
RWB-E1-001.9: Implement apply. Write the 14 rows in a single transaction, each carrying the valid from date given on the load. Do not delete the version that was in force; reference data is versioned, and AC7 requires the rows already in force to survive when a later load is refused.
RWB-E1-001.10: No application code in this step. It checks that the dictionary can be read by the people who will rely on it. Run a query against the view v_data_dictionary, filtering on the entity loan_account and the field days_past_due, which holds the number of days an account is overdue. Run it as a plain SQL query against the DEV database, not through the application, because the point is to prove the view itself returns the joined row. The same query is what a developer will use later whenever they need to know where a field comes from.
RWB-E1-001.11: The query must return one row holding field_id DF-ACC-014, data_type NUMBER, physical_type integer, source system Core bank (ALS) via COLLINS, source field DELAY_DAYS, data product DP01, refresh cycle DAILY and owner role RW-DATASTEW, with the owner user ID of DP01. If any of those come back empty, the sys_fields insert in step 3 is incomplete and the story is not done.

RWB-E1-013.1: A person starts this, the reference data administrator, who holds the Reference data C right. They upload the file of six measure definitions to the existing endpoint POST /admin/reference-loads with table set to measure_definition. The Tribe lead agrees the definitions and is named as approver on each row; the administrator only loads them. Your work is MeasureDefinitionLoadHandler, which the P4 reference load service calls for this table code. It receives the parsed rows and the valid from date. Each row carries the measure code, name, formula, data product, unit, definition version, approver and approval date, so the formula of a measure is data and never code.
RWB-E1-013.2: This runs automatically in MeasureDefinitionLoadHandler, before anything is written. Check every row for a measure code, a name, a formula, a data product, a unit, an approver and an approval date. One missing value refuses the entire file, including the rows that are correct, and no definition version is put in force. Answer with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field that is empty. Refusing in full is the rule for every reference load, because a half loaded definition set would let a measure publish under a formula nobody approved. Write unit tests for a good file of six rows and for a file whose TIME_IN_STAGE row has no formula.
RWB-E1-013.3: A scheduled job does this with nobody present. Build ReportingExtractJob and schedule it in Quartz for 01:30 Asia/Bangkok every night. It reads case facts for the previous business date by calling CaseReportingApi.caseFacts, which belongs to module P3 and returns the case ID, product group, route code, stage code, queue code, entry date, stage clock start, closed date and status. It reads payments by calling RecoveryDataApi.paymentsSinceEntry in module P1. Use these two interfaces only, since reporting never queries another module's tables. Call RecoveryDataApi.loadStatus as well, so the job knows whether the loads of that business date passed their checks before it computes anything.
RWB-E1-013.4: The job computes the values itself. Build MeasureCalculators, one calculator per measure code, and let each one read only the facts the interfaces returned. Ask MeasureCatalog.inForce for the definitions valid on the business date, then run the calculator for each measure code it names: counts of cases by route code, by age band and by queue; realized recovery as the sum of payments since entry; the median time in stage; and the median turnaround per route. Age bands are reference rows, so read the band edges from that list rather than writing day numbers into the code. Test each calculator against the synthetic case set, where the answers are known in advance.
RWB-E1-013.5: The job writes the results, with no person involved. One computed number becomes one row in measure_snapshot, so a count of cases by route for one product gives one row per route value. Each row carries the measure code, the definition version used, the business date, the product group, the dimension code, the dimension value, the value, the case count and the time it was published. The unique key across measure code, definition version, business date, product group, dimension code and dimension value is what makes a rerun safe: the same computation replaces its own row rather than adding a second copy. Build MeasureSnapshotEntity and the migration V1_013__measures.sql for both new tables.
RWB-E1-013.6: The job decides this from configuration, not from a person. Read the property rwb.reporting.baseline-date, set to 2026-11-27, and when the business date being computed matches it, set is_baseline and frozen to true on the rows written. Protect frozen rows in two places. In the service, skip any row already frozen when a date is rerun. In the database, add a trigger to measure_snapshot that refuses an UPDATE or DELETE where frozen is true; a trigger is code the database runs by itself on a write, so even a direct SQL statement cannot change a frozen value. Test that an update of a frozen row fails and that a rerun answers MSG-P9-001.
RWB-E1-013.7: The job does this at the end of its run. Build DataLakeWriter, which writes the INT-19 extract files through the integration adapters into the data lake load area. Each file carries the business date, the freshness stamp and a trailer holding the record count, so a reader can tell whether the data is complete and how old it is. When the load area does not answer, hold the extract, send an alert to the operations channel with MSG-GEN-006, and send the files on the next JOB-15 run; the snapshot rows are already written in the Workbench, so nothing is lost. Record the run on the job monitor with its row count, start time and end time.
RWB-E1-013.8: A person owns this part and no Workbench code runs in it. The Reporting and BI analyst builds the Power BI data set over the extract files in the data lake and sets it to refresh at 07:30, after JOB-15 has written the night's files. The report reads the previous day's rows and the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 together, which is why every extract has to carry the baseline rows unchanged. Your side of the handover is the extract: a stable file layout, the business date, the freshness stamp and the trailer count. The story is done when the analyst has refreshed the data set once in SIT from your extract.

RWB-E1-025.1: Three people do this away from the Workbench, and no code runs. The center of excellence analyst draws up the six document types, demand letter, court notice, appraisal report, title deed, settlement agreement and guarantor notice, with their 26 fields in total. A legal counsel user signs for Legal and a Head of NPA user signs for NPA, each with a user ID and a date, and both sign-offs sit on every row of the load file. Classification and extraction cannot be built against a list that may still change, so the sign-off is the gate. Your code never creates this list; it holds what the file carries and refuses any row without both sign-offs.
RWB-E1-025.2: A person uploads the file, the reference data administrator, who holds the Reference data C right. The request is multipart form data on the existing P4 endpoint POST /admin/reference-loads: the file itself in the Excel template, table set to DOCUMENT_TYPE and validFrom set to 30 November 2026. The response is a ReferenceLoad holding the load ID, the table, the valid from date, the status and the row count. Your work here is to add DOCUMENT_TYPE to the table codes the endpoint accepts and to parse the template columns into rows. A caller without Reference data C is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002, and with the feature flag rwb.dochub.doctypes off the table code is refused.
RWB-E1-025.3: This handover happens automatically inside the service. P4 owns the endpoint and P5 owns the document types, so P5 supplies a class that P4 calls. Write DocumentTypeLoader as your implementation of the published interface ReferenceTableLoader: tableCode returns DOCUMENT_TYPE, validateAndStage takes the load ID, the table version, the valid from date and the parsed rows, and approve takes the load ID and the approver's user ID. P4 picks the implementation by matching the table code in the request, so no change inside P4 is needed beyond listing the code. Keep every rule about document types in your class, since P4 knows nothing about retention classes or sign-offs.
RWB-E1-025.4: Your code runs these checks with no person involved. In validateAndStage, read every row and test it: the type code appears once in the file, label_en is present, write_once is set, retention_class is a value in LOV-RETENTION, the field list holds at least one field, and both the Legal and the NPA sign-off carry a user ID and a date. Read LOV-RETENTION through the P4 list service, which holds LEGAL10Y and GENERAL05Y, rather than querying the lov_value table yourself. Collect the errors of every row before you answer, because the response names each failing row with its error. Unit test a valid file of six rows first.
RWB-E1-025.5: Your code decides this, and nobody is asked. One failing row refuses the whole file, so a file of six types with a missing NPA sign-off on the sixth writes none of the six. Answer with 422 and MSG-P3-027 naming the table, the error and the row number. The version already in force keeps every row it had and the readers keep returning it, so work in flight is untouched by a bad file. Set the load status to REFUSED and write nothing to document_type. Test this with the guarantor notice row missing its NPA sign-off, and with a file holding retention class KEEP99 and a repeated court notice type code.
RWB-E1-025.6: Your code writes the rows automatically once every row has passed. Insert the six rows into document_type with table_version set to the version name in the file, DOCTYPE-2026.11, and valid_from set to the date on the load. The load status becomes LOADED, which means written and waiting for approval. DocumentTypeCatalog must not return these rows yet, so the readers in RWB-E1-024, RWB-E1-050 and RWB-E1-053 keep seeing the earlier version until approval comes. The unique constraint on doc_type_code and table_version is what refuses a second load of the same version with 409. Keep the load ID on each row, so the approval can find them.
RWB-E1-025.7: A second person acts here. The approver holds the Reference data A right, which the permission matrix gives to no role today and which is assumed granted to the legal counsel who owns the table. They call POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve with the load ID in the path and get back the ReferenceLoad with status APPROVED. Build the separation of duty check inside approve: compare the approver's user ID with the user who loaded the version and refuse with 409 and MSG-P7-002 when they match, even if that user holds both rights. Refuse with 409 as well when the load is not in status LOADED. Approving an approved load returns it unchanged.
RWB-E1-025.8: Your code does all of this inside approve. Set the load status to APPROVED, and set valid_to on the rows of the version that was in force to the day before the new valid from date, so two versions never overlap. A version takes effect on its own date and not on its approval date: a version approved in December with valid from 1 January 2027 is returned only from that day, and a read on 31 December still gets the earlier one. Build that date rule into DocumentTypeCatalogService, which holds a five minute cache, and clear the cache on approval so the new version is not hidden behind stale entries.

RWB-E1-038.1: A person prepares this by hand, the reference data administrator. The source is the Delegation of authority matrix, where one limit can cover several decision codes and regulation items, so the file holds one row per limit and decision code, and the same limits are repeated for product MORTGAGE and for product SSME. Build the converter template that guides this work: amounts in THB million become baht, No limit becomes an empty cell, Up to X percent becomes loss_pct_limit, At least X percent against fair market value becomes min_price_pct_fmv, and Once and Twice become max_delay_count. Amounts are never converted or rounded later, so the file carries baht with two decimals.
RWB-E1-038.2: The same person uploads the file to the endpoint built in RWB-E1-043. The request is multipart: the file, table set to delegation_limit, and the valid from date, with the version name carried in the file, for example DOA-2026.11. The response is 201 with a ReferenceLoad holding the load ID, the table, the valid from date, status Loaded and the row count. The caller sends an Idempotency-Key header, so a repeated request creates no second load. The endpoint refuses a caller without the Reference data C right with 403 and MSG-P4-002, a version name that already exists with 409 and MSG-GEN-004, and a file that fails validation with 422 and MSG-P1-002.
RWB-E1-038.3: Your code runs this with nobody watching. Write DelegationLimitLoader and check the whole file before you write anything: every decision code, approval level and product is a known value in LOV-DECISION, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL and LOV-PRODUCT, no required field is empty, no two rows repeat the same decision, regulation item, product, level and limits, and the highest principal limit of a level does not fall below the limit of the level under it. One failure refuses the whole file with MSG-P1-002 and leaves the version in force untouched. When every row passes, insert the rows with the version name and status Loaded, which means written and not yet usable by the lookup.
RWB-E1-038.4: A second person acts here, the Risk and model risk officer. The load response carries a difference report showing what the new version changes against the version in force, and that officer reads it before approving. They then call POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve with the load ID in the path. Build no screen for this; the officer sees the difference report and the approval result in the endpoint responses until SCR-41 arrives in Epic 8. The approver role for this table is held in the parameter rwb.refload.approver.delegation_limit, set to RW-RISK, so read the role from the parameter rather than writing RW-RISK into your code.
RWB-E1-038.5: Four things happen automatically in one call, and their order matters. Reuse ReferenceLoadApprovalService, shared with RWB-E1-037. Check the approver's role against the parameter and refuse with 403 and MSG-P4-002 otherwise, then check that the approver is not the user who loaded the file and refuse with 409 and MSG-P7-002. Next write one decision log entry with decision code AC-VERS and no case ID, naming the version and its valid from date. Only then close the previous version by setting valid_to to the day before the new valid from, and mark the version Approved. A failed decision log write answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and leaves the load Loaded.
RWB-E1-038.6: Another module calls your code, and no person is involved. The approval router of RWB-E2-013 calls the published interface DelegationOfAuthority.lowestLevel, which you offer from package recovery.access.delegation. The DelegationRequest carries the decision code, the regulation item, the product group, applies_when, the principal in baht, the loss percentage and loss amount, the price percentages, the received percentage, the delay count, the term in years, the related party flag and the decision date. The regulation item is in the request because one decision code can cover several items, for example D7.5 covering items 2.1.4, 2.1.6 and 2.1.9, and each item has its own limits. Your lookup never guesses the item.
RWB-E1-038.7: Your code computes the answer. Write DelegationLookupService to read the delegation_limit rows whose valid from and valid to span the decision date for that decision code, regulation item, product and applies_when, then test them from L6, the lowest level, upward to L1, the Board. The first level with a row that covers every figure in the request is the answer. Where a level has two rows, the level qualifies when either row is met. An empty limit column means no limit on that figure. Return the status COVERED, the approval level, the row IDs used, the version name, and the holder and substitute user IDs. The lookup index serves this read.
RWB-E1-038.8: Your code handles this case automatically. When no row at any level covers the request, for example a hire purchase decision before the chapter 8 limits are supplied, answer with status NOT_COVERED in place of a level, so the caller holds the item rather than letting it through. Raise an incident through the ACE incident path to the RW-RISK queue naming the decision code and the product group, with MSG-P7-010 as the message the user sees. Do not fall back to L1 and approve nothing. Test this with a request for decision D6.4, item 2.1.1 and product HIRE_PURCHASE against a version that holds no hire purchase rows.

RWB-E1-050.1: A scheduled job calls your code, with no person involved. JOB-12 Document intake already exists and runs every 15 minutes in business hours; this story adds one step to it, classifyStep, placed after the OCR step that RWB-E1-049 built. Write ClassifyStep as that step and wire it into the job after ocrStep, so it only ever sees items whose text has already been read. That order is what makes the selection in the next step possible, because classification needs the OCR text. With the feature flag rwb.dochub.classify off, the step is skipped and every scanned item goes to review with reason LOW_CONFIDENCE, so the job has to run with the step absent.
RWB-E1-050.2: Your step picks its own work, with no person choosing. Query document_intake for items whose ocr_status is DONE, whose predicted_type is empty and which carry no document type already, and lock each row as you take it, so two runs of the job cannot classify the same item twice. An upload arrives with its type named by the person who uploaded it, so it is skipped and no model call is made for it. Items in RESCAN or FAILED are not selected either, because their ocr_status is not DONE. Add the index ix_intake_classify on ocr_status for rows where predicted_type and review_reason are both empty, so the query stays cheap as the table grows.
RWB-E1-050.3: Your step does this itself, before any text leaves the document hub. Read the page count from the parameter CLASSIFY_MAX_PAGES in document_hub_parameter, set to 3, and take the text of that many pages from document_text. Then build TextMasker, which calls the ACE PII masking service and replaces every national ID number, account number and phone number with a token, a short placeholder that keeps the text readable while carrying no personal value. Only the masked text goes to the model. Test this with a synthetic page holding a national ID number and an account number, and check that the stub received tokens in place of both. Never log the text.
RWB-E1-050.4: This is an automatic call to a model outside your code. Write ClassifierClient with one method, classify, taking the masked text, the type labels and a timeout, and implement it as ModelGatewayClassifier over the P10 model gateway on the route named in rwb.dochub.classify.model-route. Read the six type codes and their labels from the document type table in force, DOCTYPE-2026.11, so the model is told which types exist as data and not from a list inside the code. The answer holds one score per type and the model version. Set the timeout from CLASSIFY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 60 seconds, and throw ClassifierTimeoutException when the model does not answer in time.
RWB-E1-050.5: Your step writes the result automatically. Sort the scores, highest first, and write to the intake item: predicted_type as the top type code, classification_confidence as its score in a numeric column with four decimals, type_candidates as the two highest scoring types with their scores, and classifier_version as the model version the gateway returned. Write the two candidates on every item, including the ones that pass the threshold, because the review queue of RWB-E1-054 offers them to a person as the two choices. Add these columns to document_intake in the migration V1_5_050__intake_classification.sql, along with classify_fallback, and add document_type and type_candidates to document.
RWB-E1-050.6: Your code decides this with no person involved. Compare the top score with the parameter CLASSIFY_THRESHOLD, which holds 0.80, and treat the threshold as inclusive, so a score of exactly 0.80 passes. Check as well that the predicted type code appears in the document type table in force. When both hold, leave review_reason empty, which is the signal that attach reads. Attach is built in RWB-E1-032 and stores the document with review_status NOT_NEEDED, so no person sees it. Because the threshold is a parameter row, raising it to 0.90 changes the outcome with no code change and no deployment, and that behavior is itself a test case.
RWB-E1-050.7: Your code sets one field and the rest follows from it. A top score under the threshold sets review_reason to LOW_CONFIDENCE and keeps the predicted type and the two candidates on the item. A type code the model returns that is not in the table in force sets review_reason to UNKNOWN_TYPE with no predicted type, and still keeps the two highest agreed types as candidates. Attach, in RWB-E1-032, reads review_reason and stores the document with review_status PENDING and write_once false, so a person can correct the type later. The document then shows on SCR-31, built in RWB-E1-054, with MSG-P5-003 and its two candidates. A model timeout sets MODEL_UNAVAILABLE the same way.
RWB-E1-050.8: A person starts this one, the center of excellence analyst, and it is no part of the nightly job. Build ClassificationEvaluationRunner to classify the labeled sample of 180 synthetic documents, 30 of each type, where the true type of each document is known. It counts how many predictions match the label and writes the accuracy, the 6 by 6 confusion matrix showing which type was predicted for each true type, and the model version, into evaluation/classification/{runDate}.json in the standard container and onto the job record. The risk and model risk officer reads that report before the step runs in production, and at least 162 of the 180 have to be correct.

RWB-E1-062.1: Two other modules produce these events, and your code creates neither. The case workflow module writes EV-01 CaseCreated when a case is opened, and the document hub writes EV-16 DocumentStored when a document is stored on an open case, carrying the document ID, the case ID, the type and the source. This story only consumes them, so nothing changes in the modules that publish them. Both events are delivered at least once and each carries an event ID, which is what makes the idempotency check in the next step possible. Your work starts at the consumer; treat these two events as the only two ways a screening run begins.
RWB-E1-062.2: Your listener does this automatically. Write ScreeningShadowListener to consume both events and call the agent orchestrator for agent SCREENING, passing a run key built from SCREENING, the case ID and the event ID joined by colons. The key makes the call idempotent, which means the same event arriving twice has the same effect as arriving once: the second delivery finds the existing run, no second model call is made, and the repeat is counted under rule R-UNI-40. The case ID on its own would not do, because one case has one run per triggering event. With the flag rwb.agent.screening-shadow off, both listeners ignore their events.
RWB-E1-062.3: Your code assembles the input, with no person involved. Write ScreeningInputAssembler to call P3 CaseQueryService.getCase, P7 InteractionLedgerReader.list for the ledger window of 180 days held in the policy, and P5 DocumentQueryService.listByCase and getFields. Every call runs as the system identity SY-AGENT, which holds Case record R and Documents R, so the agent reads no more than those rights allow. Mask the personal fields before the text leaves, which here means the interaction summaries and the document field values. The model call then goes out under the approved policy SCREENING P1 with the approved prompt PR1 and a 60 second timeout. Prompts and responses are never written to logs.
RWB-E1-062.4: A guardrail in your code tests the model's answer before anything is stored. The output schema screening-v1 says each proposal holds a code in the range X1 to X7, an array of reasons, source references pointing at interaction or document IDs, a confidence, and, for an X1 proposal, the ID of the preceding contact. Build ScreeningRuleChecks to apply the schema and the added rule checks. A code outside the list fails the check named SCHEMA, and the run is stored with status GUARDRAIL_FAILED and fallback true. An X1 proposal that names no preceding contact, while the ledger holds one in the 30 days before, fails the check named SCHEMA_RULE.
RWB-E1-062.5: Your code asks another component, and nobody decides by hand. Write ScreeningOwnerResolver to call P3 RuleEvaluator.ownerFor with the route set Deviations, the event OWNER_ASSIGNED and the proposed deviation code, running as SY-RULES. The answer is the owner role held in rule rows R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06, which the center of excellence maintains as data, so an owner change is a rule row change and not a code change. Store the role with the proposal, so the evaluation can show who each proposal would have gone to. A proposed code with no rule row takes owner role RW-TEAMMGR and is marked unmapped, since five rows cover seven codes.
RWB-E1-062.6: Your code writes the run and stops there. Compare each proposal's confidence with the floor of 0.80 held in the agent policy and mark the ones below it with the marker review. Write one agent_run row holding the agent code and version, the prompt and model versions, the case ID, the autonomy mode SHADOW, the trigger event, the idempotency key, the status, the fallback flag, the guardrail result, the output, the confidence, the latency, the token counts and the cost. Shadow mode means stored and acted on by nobody: write no deviation row, leave deviation_open false, set no contact stop, pause no clock, and never call the S8 deviation service.
RWB-E1-062.7: A person starts this, the center of excellence analyst, who holds Rules and parameters C. They call POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-evaluations naming agent SCREENING and sample SCREEN-S1, which is the business analysts' review of 200 Epic 1 cases, one row per case and code with an expected value of Y or N. Your code creates an agent_evaluation_run row with status RUNNING. Refuse a sample with no labeled rows with 422 and MSG-P10-002, and a second evaluation of the same agent and sample while one is running with 409 and MSG-P10-003. A role without the right is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002.
RWB-E1-062.8: Your scorer runs on its own once the evaluation starts. Write ScreeningScorer to compare the proposals at or above the confidence floor with the Y and N labels in the sample, code by code. Proposals marked review are left out of that comparison and counted on their own in review_count, a column this story adds to agent_evaluation_run in the migration V10_005__evaluation_review_count.sql. For each code X1 to X7, write one agent_evaluation row holding the sample size, the true positive, false positive and false negative counts, and precision and recall computed from them. Precision is the share of proposals that were right; recall is the share of labeled deviations the agent found.

RWB-E2-006.1: A person starts this, the restructuring officer, on the treatment the plan belongs to. SCR-14 Treatment record already exists, and this story adds a read only pack to it. Build CreditPackPanel as a React component on that screen, shown while the treatment is submitted and the case is in route state AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL. The panel gives a copy action per field, because the officer has to put these values into NLEADS, a separate bank system the Workbench cannot call. The case owner may also open the pack on cases in their scope. Opening the pack writes nothing and takes no decision.
RWB-E2-006.2: The screen makes this call automatically when the officer opens the pack. The endpoint GET /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-pack is new in this story and recorded in the additions file, with the treatment ID in the path and nothing in the body. It is read only, so it needs no idempotency key and a repeated call changes nothing. The response is a CreditPack holding the case number, the product group, the accounts, the collateral, the plan terms, the required level, the documents and the messages. Build CreditPackController for this endpoint and for the result endpoint. A source interface that does not answer gives 503 with MSG-GEN-006.
RWB-E2-006.3: Your code does this, with nobody involved. Check two things before reading: the caller holds the Treatment and offer right at level R, and the case is inside the caller's scope. A missing right answers 403 with MSG-P4-002; a case outside scope answers 404 with MSG-P4-003, the same answer as a case that does not exist, so the response tells the caller nothing about cases they may not see. Then build CreditPackService to gather the pack through published interfaces only: TreatmentQuery.get for the treatment and its terms, the P1 interfaces for accounts, balances, collateral and the latest valuation, and CaseDocuments.byTypes for the documents. Query no other module's tables.
RWB-E2-006.4: Two reference reads happen automatically here. Call DelegationQuery.requiredLevel in module P7 with the decision code, the product group and the amount, and it returns the level the delegation of authority sets for that plan, for example L6 under item 2.1.1. Read the document types that belong in the pack from NleadsChecklist, the versioned rule rows holding the NLEADS pack checklist, and pass those types to CaseDocuments.byTypes. Both values are data rows: the checklist is agreed by the business lead with Legal, and the limits are loaded by Risk. Write neither the level nor the list of document types into your code, since both change with no release.
RWB-E2-006.5: The service builds the response automatically. Every field is returned ready to copy, so the officer types nothing: the case number, the product group, each account with its principal, interest, total balance, days past due and data as of date, the collateral with its appraised value and appraisal date, and the plan terms. For each checklist type, return the document ID and a link when the case holds one, and mark it missing with MSG-P2-009 when it does not. Compute the age in days of each input from its data as of date, and where an input is past its age limit of one business day, attach MSG-P7-006 with the day count.
RWB-E2-006.6: This happens outside the Workbench and no code of yours runs. NLEADS has no interface, so the officer opens NLEADS, copies the pack values into it, opens the documents from the links, and submits. NLEADS gives back a reference at once and the credit decision later, with the level that approved it. Build no call to NLEADS, not even a stub meant for later use, because the guardrail for this story is that the Workbench never calls NLEADS. The wait between submission and result is open ended, so the treatment sits in state submitted and the case stays in route state AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL until the officer comes back with the result.
RWB-E2-006.7: The same person returns to SCR-14 and types the outcome. Build CreditResultForm as a React component with fields for the NLEADS reference, the result, the approval level, the result date and the reason, each showing its own field error. It posts to the new endpoint POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/credit-result with an If-Match header holding the treatment version the officer read. The reference is 1 to 30 letters, digits and dashes, the result is APPROVED or REFUSED, the level is L1 to L6, and the reason is 1 to 1,000 characters and required when the result is REFUSED. The case owner may record a result on cases in their scope.
RWB-E2-006.8: Your code runs the checks and the first write automatically. Refuse an empty reference or an empty reason on a refusal with 422 and MSG-GEN-001, a result date after today with 422 and MSG-GEN-002, an approval level below the level the plan needs with 409 and MSG-P2-018, a result already recorded with 409 and MSG-P2-010, a case not awaiting credit approval with 409 and MSG-P3-005, and an If-Match version that no longer matches with 409 and MSG-GEN-004. Then call DecisionLogWriter.write with decision D5, the final call and the NLEADS reference in the actions. Write that entry before the treatment changes, and change nothing when DecisionLogUnavailableException is thrown.
RWB-E2-006.9: Your code writes the outcome once the decision log entry is in. Call TreatmentCommands.recordCreditResult with the treatment ID, the command and the version the officer read, so two officers saving at the same time end with one saved result and one 409 with MSG-GEN-004. The treatment then holds nleads_ref, credit_result, credit_result_reason, credit_result_at, approval_level, the decision log ID and its state, APPROVED or REFUSED. The four new treatment columns are added by the treatment owner in its own migration, with a check that the reason is not empty when the result is REFUSED. Then call CaseEvents.raise with CREDIT_APPROVED or CREDIT_DECLINED, which hands the case move to P3.
RWB-E2-006.10: The rules component and the case workflow module do this on the event you raised, and you build none of it here. On CREDIT_APPROVED, rule R-RES-11 moves the route state from AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL to OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER and the offer goes to the customer with a 14 day validity. On CREDIT_DECLINED, rule R-RES-12 moves it to DECLINED_BY_CREDIT and records the reason, then R-RES-14 moves it to BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION on DECLINE_RECORDED and the case appears in the case owner's queue. Your tests check the route state and the queue after each event, since this is how the officer and the case owner see a credit result.

RWB-E2-018.1: A person starts this, the restructuring officer, or the case owner on a case in their scope. The agreement document already exists on the case, generated and stored in the document hub by RWB-E2-017. Build SendForSignatureDialog as a React component on SCR-14 Treatment record, shown while the treatment is approved and the offer is with the customer. The dialog lets the officer pick the document and the party who signs, and the request list beside it shows each request with its status. The customer never signs in the Workbench and has no login there; they sign in EasyApp or on paper at a branch.
RWB-E2-018.2: Your code decides which methods the officer may choose. Read signature_basis from the template the document was generated from, which Legal counsel sets in RWB-E1-034 to either E_SIGNATURE_ALLOWED or WET_INK_REQUIRED. When the basis allows it, offer E_SIGNATURE, BRANCH and PAPER; when Legal requires wet ink, offer only BRANCH and PAPER. Apply the same rule again on the server in SignatureService.create, because the dialog alone cannot hold the rule. A request with method E_SIGNATURE for a wet ink template is refused with 409 and MSG-P6-009 naming the template, and nothing reaches EasyApp.
RWB-E2-018.3: Your code calls the check built in RWB-E2-022 before it creates anything. A signature request sent to a customer is an outbound contact, so it passes the same conduct check as any other contact. An open deviation with a contact stop refuses the request with 409 and MSG-P6-001 naming the deviation, for example X2 Vulnerable customer or hardship. A legal hold on the case refuses it with 409 and MSG-P3-004. In both cases no signature_request row is written and nothing goes to the outbox. Test this with an open X2 carrying a contact stop, and check that the EasyApp stub received no call.
RWB-E2-018.4: Your code writes the row and queues the send automatically. Insert a signature_request row with the case ID, the treatment ID, the document ID, the party ID, the method, the status, and expires_at taken from the treatment's valid_until, so the request ends with the offer and not on a date of its own. Create the table in the migration V2_018__signature_request.sql with a unique index on external_ref and an index on treatment ID and status. For E_SIGNATURE, write the send to the outbox in place of calling EasyApp inline; JOB-11 Outbox sender delivers it through EsignPort with a retry limit of 5, and an unavailable path answers 201 with status QUEUED and MSG-GEN-006.
RWB-E2-018.5: This happens outside the Workbench. The customer opens EasyApp and signs there, and EasyApp applies the bank signature using the bank signing certificate held in the key store. The Workbench never holds the private key and never calls EasyApp directly; the ACE common module owns that path under INT-34. EasyApp returns the signed PDF, the result and the time of signing through the same path. Your side of it is the method the ACE module calls, SignatureResultListener.onEasyAppResult, taking the external reference, the result, the signed PDF bytes and the signing time. Test everything behind a stub of that path, using synthetic PDFs.
RWB-E2-018.6: Three writes happen automatically in your listener, within 60 seconds of the result arriving. Call DocumentHubApi.addVersion to store the signed PDF as a new version of the same document with write_once true, which means a stored version can never be changed or replaced, only followed by a further version. Set the signature request to status SIGNED with signed_at and signed_document_id. Then call TreatmentApi.recordSignature with signed true and the method used, which is how the case moves; P3 owns the treatment fields and this story writes none of them directly. Make the listener idempotent on the external reference and the result, so a repeated result stores no second document.
RWB-E2-018.7: Three actors appear here and only the last one calls your endpoint. The customer signs the printed agreement at a branch. The branch scan reaches the case through JOB-12 Document intake, which already exists, so this story does not load the image. The restructuring officer then calls POST /signature-requests/{requestId}/result with result SIGNED, the scanned document ID and the signed date, and your code sets the request to SIGNED, links the scan to the generated agreement with DocumentHubApi.linkSigned, and calls TreatmentApi.recordSignature with method BRANCH. A result recorded with no scanned document is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 naming the signed document.
RWB-E2-018.8: The officer records the result as in the branch path, with method PAPER and the scan of the signed contract, and the rest is P3's work. Pass the signature basis with the recorded signature, because wet ink is what sends a mortgage deed in lieu to the collateral inspection before the transfer. On that event P3 moves the case to WITH_FIELD_INSPECTION under rule R-DIL-18, and later to the Land Office transfer under R-DIL-27. Build neither the inspection nor the transfer, since both are Epic 3 screens. Your test checks the route state after the result, using a deed in lieu treatment whose contract template carries WET_INK_REQUIRED.
RWB-E2-018.9: Two closing paths run automatically. When EasyApp returns DECLINED, set the request to status DECLINED and call TreatmentApi.recordSignature with signed false, which lets the route set's decline rule return the case. When the offer validity passes with no signature, P3 raises OFFER_EXPIRED and calls SignatureApi.cancel, which you implement in SignatureApiService to set the request to EXPIRED. A signing result that arrives after that keeps the request EXPIRED, makes no call to recordSignature, and goes to the exception queue on SCR-09. A result naming an external reference that matches no request goes to the same queue with the reason unknown signature request.

RWB-E2-034.1: The outbox built in RWB-TE-006 does this automatically. An outbox holds each published event in the database and delivers it to its consumers, retrying until the consumer succeeds, so no event is lost while your code is down. Your work is to add a consumer named ledger-channels to rwb.integration.outbox.consumers and have it take seven events: EV-20 InstructionIssued, EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted, EV-14 NoticeDispatched, EV-15 NoticeDelivered, EV-10 TreatmentApproved, EV-25 ProceedsMatched and EV-26 LoadCompleted for the COLLINS load. Delivery is at least once, so the same event can arrive twice. EV-02 CaseAllocated and EV-04 CaseTransferred stay with the consumer of RWB-E1-067.
RWB-E2-034.2: Your listener runs with no person involved. Write LedgerChannelListener and call IdempotencyGuard.firstTime with the consumer name ledger-channels and the event's idempotency key before you do any work. Idempotent means a repeated delivery has the same effect as the first one: the guard answers false on a key it has seen, the listener acknowledges the delivery, writes nothing, and the hit count for that key goes up by one under rule R-UNI-40. On a first delivery, pass the event to LedgerChannelMapper. With the flag rwb.integration.ledger-channels off, acknowledge all seven events and write nothing.
RWB-E2-034.3: Your mapper turns one event into one ledger command, automatically. Write LedgerChannelMapper with a method per event type: InstructionIssued becomes a HANDOVER entry with channel PORTAL and direction OUTBOUND, PartnerResultSubmitted becomes PARTNER_RESULT with channel PORTAL and direction INBOUND, NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered each become a LETTER entry carrying the delivery status and the barcode, TreatmentApproved becomes OFFER linked to the treatment, and ProceedsMatched becomes PAYMENT linked to the proceeds. All of these carry source WORKBENCH. Read the facts you need through NoticeQuery.byId, InstructionQuery.byId and CaseQuery.byId, never from those modules' tables. Hold the contact point as a reference and never copy the number itself.
RWB-E2-034.4: This path runs as a job step and not through the mapper. Write EfsContactOutcomeImporter as a step of JOB-01 COLLINS load check and intake, running under SY-DATALOAD after the load passes its checks. Call EfsContactHistory.outcomesFor for the business date, then for each row call CaseQuery.openCaseIdsForAccount and keep only rows whose account sits on an open case. Keep only the action codes on the EFS ledger outcome list, a reference table loaded by the reference data administrator. Each kept row becomes a CONTACT entry with source EFS and the channel from its list row. Write an import summary counting rows read, written, excluded by the list and not on a case.
RWB-E2-034.5: This is a change to code another story owns, so have its code owners review it. RWB-E1-067 already maps EV-02 CaseAllocated and EV-04 CaseTransferred to CASE_ALLOCATED and CASE_TRANSFERRED entries, and those two events keep their own consumer. Write HolderEnricher inside that mapper in recovery.dataengine.ledger to fill from_holder_ref and to_holder_ref on the same entry, in the form USER followed by the user ID.
