For each merge code on the template, read merge_field.source_entity and merge_field.source_field, then call the published interface of the module that owns that source, such as PartyApi.contactPoints for a contact point or RecoveryDataApi.caseBalance for the balance. Personal values are held as tokens, which are placeholders carrying no name or address. The ACE PII service exchanges a token for the real value and writes one access event per field to PII Kafka. Clear values go into the PDF alone: the merge snapshot keeps tokens, and logs, tests and prompts hold no personal data.
RWB-E1-052.5: The service decides this with no person in the loop. The column merge_field.is_required says which values must be present. When one of them is empty, write the notice row in state Held with hold_reason set to that field, store no document, and call CaseWorkflowApi.raiseTask with task code Complete notice data and the case owner as owner role, carrying MSG-P6-007, which names the notice, the case and the field. Generation ends there: no render, no decision log entry, no document. AC3 is the test, with party P-0001 holding no postal address contact point and hold reason POSTAL_ADDRESS.
RWB-E1-052.6: The renderer does this. Build LetterRenderer to fill the DOCX body named by template.body_ref with the resolved values and render a PDF. The footer carries four items in order: case number, template code, template version and generation date, which AC1 shows as RC-2026-000123 DEMAND-MTG v2 2026-11-25. Use the ACE document rendering library, or docx4j with PDF export where ACE has none, which needs dependency approval under NFR-054. Thai text has to come out correctly, and the done condition is a generated PDF from the synthetic set opening in a standard PDF reader with its Thai shown.
RWB-E1-052.7: The service writes this through DecisionLogApi.write from P7, built in RWB-E1-027. The entry carries decision code D7.1, rule R-LIT-03, the template code and version, and an inputs reference pointing at the merge snapshot. It is written before the document is stored, which is the order section 12 fixes. A failed write means no notice at all: the call fails with MSG-P7-003, no notice row and no document are created, and an incident is raised under R-UNI-39. When the account data product is stale, the entry records the data date used, 2026-11-24 in AC7, and the result carries MSG-P1-001 naming the product and that date.
RWB-E1-052.8: The service calls the document hub; no person uploads anything. Call DocumentHubApi.storeGenerated with the case, the party, the document type and the PDF bytes. P5 owns the document table, so write nothing to it from this module. Write-once means the stored file is never replaced, and a correction is a new notice with a new document. AC1 expects source GENERATED and write_once true on the stored PDF. A failed document store rolls the notice back, and the decision log entry already written is followed by a correcting entry under R-UNI-24 rather than being changed in place.
RWB-E1-052.9: The service finishes the work in one transaction. Migration V1_052__notice_generation.sql alters the existing notice table to add party_id, template_id and hold_reason, adds the check constraint on state, and adds the unique index ux_notice_generation on case_id, notice_type, party_id and the date part of created_at. That index is the idempotency key: a repeat on the same business date hands back the first notice and creates no second one, which AC6 tests. Sent type is NPL for a case at 90 days past due or more, taken from LOV-SENT-TYPE. NoticeGeneratedPublisher writes NoticeGenerated, EV-13 with noticeId, caseId, type and templateVersion, to the outbox in that same transaction.

RWB-E1-064.1: A person starts this. The reference data administrator, RW-REFADM with Reference data C, submits one file covering every field through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads with table sys_fields, and it is approved through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve with Reference data A. The data steward prepares the file from s2t.txt and the Logical Data Model. The attributes in it land in the new sys_fields columns owner_role, refresh_cycle, late_behavior and interface_id, which the Flyway migration of this story adds. The rows themselves already exist: RWB-E1-001 seeded sys_objects and sys_fields with the entities and fields of the recovery schema, so this load fills attributes rather than creating fields.
RWB-E1-064.2: The loader does this on its own. Build the published interface DataDictionaryLoader with apply taking the load version, a valid from date and the rows. Validate the whole file before writing anything: one field missing one attribute refuses the load in full with MSG-P1-002 and the first failing check, and the dictionary in force is left as it was. AC6 shows the form of that check, refresh_cycle missing for DF-COL-005. On success, write the attributes and one sys_field_version row per field holding the definition as jsonb with its version number, change reason, changed_at and changed_by. The migration seeds version 1 for every field.
RWB-E1-064.3: DataContractService does this as part of the same load, with no person involved. Group the fields by sys_fields.interface_id to build one data_contract row per source system, holding contract_code, source_system, interface_id, contract_version, status DRAFT and the count of mapped fields. The Flyway migration creates data_contract with a status check of DRAFT, PUBLISHED or SUPERSEDED and unique contract_code with contract_version. A data contract is the written agreement with the system that sends the data. The background of section 7 shows the shape: DC-ALS for Core bank (ALS) covering INT-01 and INT-02, DRAFT with 32 mapped fields.
RWB-E1-064.4: A developer or an analyst reads this. Build DataDictionaryController with GET /admin/data-dictionary/fields taking product, entity, field, sourceSystem, page and size, returning DataDictionaryFieldPage of DataDictionaryField with fieldId, entity, fieldName, dataType, physicalType, mandatory, listCode, sourceSystem, sourceField, refreshCycle, ownerRole, lateBehavior, interfaceId, isPersonal, version and versionDate. Authorization is Reference data R. AC1 reads loan_account.days_past_due and expects DF-ACC-014 to show type NUMBER, physical type integer, source field DELAY_DAYS and late behavior of keeping the previous value and marking DP01 stale. Other modules read the same values through DataDictionaryQuery rather than this endpoint.
RWB-E1-064.5: A person does both halves of this, and the first half happens outside the system: the data steward sends the contract to the system owner by their own means. The steward, RW-DATASTEW with Reference data U, then records confirmedByRole, confirmedOn and confirmationDocumentId with PATCH /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}. Build the PATCH with an If-Match header carrying the version the caller read. That is optimistic locking: the write is accepted only while the row has not changed since that read, and a later version answers 409 with MSG-GEN-004. An empty field answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001. AC2 records the ALS confirmation on 2026-11-12 with document DOC-SYN-0640.
RWB-E1-064.6: The data steward makes the call and the check sits in code. Build POST /admin/data-contracts/{contractId}/publish with an Idempotency-Key header, so a repeated call returns the first result. DataContractService refuses a contract that has no recorded confirmation with 409 and MSG-P1-021, which reads that the data contract for the system cannot be published until its system owner confirms it, and the contract stays DRAFT. AC4 tests this with DC-EFS for EFS. Authorization is Reference data U. This refusal is what keeps a load from depending on a source field nobody has agreed to send.
RWB-E1-064.7: The service does this inside the publish call. Set status PUBLISHED with published_at and published_by on the contract version. AC2 expects DC-ALS at contract version 1 PUBLISHED with its confirmation date. A published contract is never edited in place afterward, so this write happens once for each contract version.
RWB-E1-064.8: The data steward makes the change and the versioning happens on its own. Build PATCH /admin/data-dictionary/fields/{fieldCode} in DataDictionaryService with the If-Match header and a reason that cannot be empty: an empty reason answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and leaves the field at its current version, which AC5 tests on DF-ACC-015. Each accepted change writes a new sys_field_version row, unique on field_id and field_version, with change_reason, changed_at and changed_by, and raises the version on sys_fields. Earlier versions stay readable with their own dates. AC3 changes DF-ACC-014 to source field DPD_DAYS and expects version 2 dated 2026-11-18.
RWB-E1-064.9: The service does this on the back of the field change, with no second call from anyone. Look up the contract holding the changed field; when its status is PUBLISHED, write a new row for the same contract_code with contract_version raised by one and status DRAFT. The published version keeps serving until the new one is confirmed and published in its turn. AC8 changes DF-ACC-014 while DC-ALS version 1 is PUBLISHED and expects version 2 as DRAFT with version 1 still in force. Section 12 gives no endpoint for this, so build it inside the field change path.

RWB-E2-008.1: No clock starts this job. Build PaymentMatchingJob as a Spring Batch job started by the LoadCompleted event, EV-26, that JOB-01 publishes for the ALS source once every check has passed. A refused or late ALS load therefore means JOB-07 does not run for that business date, and no missed payment is raised from stale data, which AC5 tests. A rerun for a business date is possible from SCR-44 and skips rows already written. The job runs under the service identity SY-DATALOAD, which holds Write-off and posting U.
RWB-E2-008.2: The job reads the data through another module's interface. Call RecoveryDataApi.paymentsLoaded with the business date, the P1 published interface, to read the payments JOB-01 wrote into account_payment for that date. This module reads neither account_payment nor loan_account nor case_account directly. Each payment carries its payment code, account, payment date, amount and data_as_of. Amounts are BigDecimal with scale 2 and are compared exactly with no rounding, because the EXACT rule carries an amount tolerance of 0 percent.
RWB-E2-008.3: The job does this for every payment on its own. Call CaseWorkflowApi.openCaseForAccount with the account, the P3 published interface, which returns the open case or nothing. With no open case, write no proceeds row and hold the payment on the data quality exception list with check References, the reference exception of DQ-012. AC4 tests this with payment PAY-90003 on account A-0999. Payments are identified in logs by payment code and account ID, and account numbers are never logged. A payment that does have an open case goes on to the plan matching of the next step.
RWB-E2-008.4: The matcher does this with no person deciding. Call TreatmentApi.runningPlans for the plans on the case and RecoveryDataApi.nextInstallmentDate for the account's due date, and read the payment_match_rule row valid on the business date through PaymentMatchRuleRepository. The EXACT row of version PM-2026.12 holds amount tolerance 0 percent, a window of 10 days before the due date and 0 days after, and grace 0 days. A payment on the plan account for the installment amount and dated inside that window matches that installment. AC7 tests both sides of the window: 10 days before matches, 11 days before does not.
RWB-E2-008.5: The job writes all three things together. Insert the proceeds row with the case, the treatment, source CUSTOMER, the amount and matched_to INSTALLMENT. Call TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid with the treatment, the proceeds ID, the due date and the amount, so that P3 raises installments_paid on the plan. Write ProceedsMatched, EV-25 with proceedsId, caseId and amount, to the outbox. All of it sits in one transaction, so none of the three can exist without the others. Add unique index ux_proceeds_account_payment on account_payment_id where it is not null, which gives one proceeds row for each ALS payment.
RWB-E2-008.6: The job writes this itself. Insert the proceeds row with matched_to UNMATCHED and no treatment, and count it in the run summary with MSG-P8-001, which names the count and the date. Build ProceedsController for GET /api/recovery/v1/proceeds with a matched query value, so matched=false returns these rows for the Credit Administration officer on SCR-28. Authorization is Write-off and posting R with scope applied, and a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002. AC3 has payment PAY-90002 of 3,000.00 THB against an installment amount of 12,500.00 THB.
RWB-E2-008.7: The detector runs after every payment of the load has been matched, with no person involved. Build MissedPaymentDetector. For each running plan, add the grace days from the parameter row to the next due date, compare that against the business date, then look for a matched payment for that due date. With no payment, write PaymentMissed, EV-12 with treatmentId, dueDate and amountDue, to the outbox. New table payment_missed_event_key, unique on treatment_id and due_date, holds one event per plan and due date, so a rerun writes no second event. Unit test the grace boundary, as section 13 build step 4 asks.
RWB-E2-008.8: Another module acts here, and nothing in this story changes a plan state. P3 consumes PaymentMissed, moves plan T-0701 from PLAN_RUNNING to PLAN_CURE_PERIOD under rule R-RES-27, and records the case movement with reason payment missed through the transfer rules of RWB-E1-021. The case owner, holding Treatment and offer R, reads the plan position on SCR-14 Treatment record and the missed payment on SCR-04 Case timeline, both on the morning after the due date passed.
RWB-E2-008.9: The job closes itself out. Write the run counts, payments read, matched, unmatched and missed events, so SCR-44 shows them, with MSG-P8-001 when unmatched payments exist and MSG-P8-002 when the job stopped because no matching rule was in force on the business date. That second case also marks JOB-07 failed with an alert to Credit Administration, which AC8 tests. Then run reconciliation REC-04, which compares the payments in the ALS load against the proceeds rows by count and by amount for the date. The done condition is a synthetic month in which every ALS payment shows as a proceeds row or a held reference exception.

RWB-E2-021.1: A person starts this. Build NoticeController with POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices taking NoticeRequest with noticeType required, partyId defaulting to the borrower and language defaulting to TH, and returning 201 Notice. Authorization is Litigation C with scope applied, so the litigation officer or the enforcement owner may call it. The controller calls NoticeApi.generate from RWB-E1-052 and adds no generation logic of its own. The Idempotency-Key header is kept for 24 hours and a repeat returns the first notice, which AC10 tests. A request with no notice type answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field.
RWB-E2-021.2: A person approves the notice on SCR-18, the screen built in RWB-E2-014, and this story builds nothing here. The notice reaches state Approved, which is the only state this story dispatches: the configuration key rwb.comms.dispatch.eligible-states is set to APPROVED, so the job of the next step picks up Approved notices alone. Holding that list in configuration rather than in code lets another state become eligible later without a release. Read the key in the job rather than writing the state name into the query.
RWB-E2-021.3: The job runs on a daily schedule at 16:00. Build ConductCheckService and call it from WinNoticeFileJob, which comes from RWB-E1-055, before each file record is written. The four checks run in order: a legal hold on the case, an open deviation carrying a contact stop, the template of the notice still being Approved, and the statutory status of the notice type. Read the hold through CaseWorkflowApi.getCaseSummary, the stops through DeviationApi.activeContactStops on S8, and the statutory notice type list from reference data. The service returns Passed or Blocked with the reason and the rule ID, and runs inside the same transaction that selects the notice for the file.
RWB-E2-021.4: The job does this with no person involved. Set the notice state to Held with hold_reason naming the cause, such as CONTACT_STOP_X1, LEGAL_HOLD or TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN, and leave it out of the WIN file. Write the decision log entry through DecisionLogApi.write with decision code D7.1 and the rule that blocked it, R-LIT-05 for a contact stop, and the ledger entry through InteractionLedgerApi.record with conduct_check set to BLOCKED. Then call CaseWorkflowApi.applyEvent so P3 routes the case. AC4 routes it to the complaint officer with MSG-P6-001 naming X1 Dispute or complaint, and AC7 shows MSG-P3-004 on the case record for a legal hold.
RWB-E2-021.5: The job and the acknowledgment handling do this; both come from RWB-E1-055, and what this story adds is the conduct result on each record and on the ledger entry. The notice is written to the INT-14 file with conduct check Passed. The WIN acknowledgment then sets the notice to Sent with its sent date and barcode, the number printed on the mail item that the later proof is matched by, and the ledger entry carries that barcode. Publish NoticeDispatched, EV-14. AC1 runs JOB-10 at 16:00 on 2026-12-14 and expects sent date 2026-12-15 with barcode RR223344556TH and conduct check PASSED.
RWB-E2-021.6: JOB-09 loads the file on its own. Add the INT-15 result column to the file reader and map its result codes to LOV-DELIVERY through the code map, which the data steward owns. Build DeliveryResultHandler: a DELIVERED record sets the notice state Delivered with callback_date and delivery_status, writes the ledger entry and publishes NoticeDelivered, EV-15. P3 then starts the NOTICE_PERIOD timer from the delivery date under R-LIT-07, so the period runs from the proof date. AC2 returns barcode RR223344556TH with call-back date 18122026 and expects the timer running from 2026-12-18.
RWB-E2-021.7: The same handler takes this branch on its own. Set the notice state Unserved with delivery_status REFUSED or UNDELIVERABLE, write one decision log entry with decision code D7.1 and rule R-LIT-09, write the ledger entry, and call CaseWorkflowApi.applyEvent with DELIVERY_FAILED so P3 transfers the case to its owner's queue with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED. No notice period timer starts. The owner sees MSG-P6-008 naming the notice type and the reason, which asks them to choose another service method. A failed decision log write leaves the notice as it was and is tried again on the next run, which AC9 tests.
RWB-E2-021.8: This step runs at the start of each JOB-10 run, before anything is written to a file. Build ProofWindowStep as the first step of the job. For each notice in state Sent, compare its sent date against the business date using the proof window of 7 days, held as a timer row rather than in code. At 7 days with no proof returned, set the notice Unserved with delivery_status PENDING and write the decision log entry with rule R-LIT-08; no notice period starts. Index ix_notice_state_sent supports that read. AC6 marks one notice Unserved at 7 days and leaves a second Sent at 6 days, so test both.
RWB-E2-021.9: A person reads the result. Build GET /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId} returning the Notice with id, caseId, documentId, noticeType, sentDate, barcode, callbackDate, deliveryStatus and sentType, with Litigation R and scope applied. A notice on a case outside the caller's scope answers 404 with MSG-P4-003 rather than telling the caller the notice exists, which AC11 tests with N-0200. SCR-18, built in RWB-E2-014, shows the Sent, Delivered and Unserved states this story sets, and SCR-04 Case timeline shows each ledger entry with its conduct check result.

RWB-E2-036.1: The caller is a model job or an agent running under its own service identity, so no person makes this call. Build the endpoint from the generated server interface for operationId postQueuesQueueidPlacements, taking PlacementRequest with caseId required as a uuid, reason required at 1 to 1,000 characters, modelOrAgent required as a caller code from the approved list, and version required at 1 to 40 characters. The acceptance criteria use identity SY-AGENT with caller MDL-SYN-PRIORITY. The code sits in folder recovery/casewf/placement even though the story is in the P2 backlog, because the queue and case tables belong to P3.
RWB-E2-036.2: The controller does this first, before any other check. Read the feature flag rwb.casewf.queue-placement, which is off by default and on only in DEV and SIT test runs. When it is off, answer 404 with MSG-P2-025, which reads that queue placement by models and agents is switched off, and change nothing: no case, no assignment and no decision log entry, which AC4 tests. The platform administrator switches the flag on once a caller has been approved. The flag has to be off in UAT and production at the release, and the tests of this story run with it on in SIT.
RWB-E2-036.3: The controller does this with no person involved. Call the common module access check so the caller's service identity passes the same test as a person: it needs Queue and allocation C in the permission matrix version in force, with scope All for service identities. Without the right, answer 403 with MSG-P4-002. The production matrix gives SY-AGENT R only, so the security administrator has to load a matrix version granting C before the first caller can work, which is what access test TC-E2-036-13 checks. No model or agent reaches a queue without passing this check.
RWB-E2-036.4: The controller does this. Reject an empty field with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 naming it, and a reason or version outside its length with MSG-GEN-002. Build ApprovedCallerList to read the configuration key rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers, which holds each caller code, its type MODEL or AGENT, and the service identity listed for it. A caller code that is not in the list for the calling identity answers 422 with MSG-P2-020 and changes nothing, which AC5 tests with MDL-SYN-UNLISTED. The list is empty at go-live: the center of excellence analyst asks for an entry and the risk and model risk officer approves it.
RWB-E2-036.5: The service does this with no person involved. Read the queue for its assignment method, caseload cap and overflow queue, and the case for its status, its current queue and its deviation_open flag. Three refusals follow, each answering 409 and changing nothing: a case already in the target queue answers MSG-P2-024, which also covers a repeated call; a closed case answers MSG-P3-005; and a case with an open deviation answers MSG-P2-021 and stays with the deviation handler under R-DEV-01. A queue or case that does not exist answers 404 with MSG-P4-003.
RWB-E2-036.6: The service builds the record itself. Fill a DecisionLogRecord with decision code D6 from LOV-DECISION, the caller identity, the reason text sent in the request, the model or agent with its version, the target queue, and a final call in the form PLACED MTG-BKK-PRI. The record is built here and written at the end of step 8, which puts it in the same transaction as the case change. AC3 checks each of those values on the entry. The reason text is the caller's own code or phrase and holds no customer data, which keeps personal data out of the log.
RWB-E2-036.7: The service calls the allocation engine; no person picks the owner. Add assignInQueue, taking the case, the queue and the source identity, to AllocationService from RWB-E1-020, reusing the owner choice, cap and overflow logic that allocate already has. The method skips owners at the caseload cap, 150 in the queue data under DL23, and picks the next owner by the queue's method, ROUND_ROBIN in the acceptance criteria. AC2 gives the case to U-5002 at 149 open cases while skipping U-5001 at 150, then places the next case in queue MTG-BKK-OVF with no owner and status NEW when both owners are at the cap.
RWB-E2-036.8: The service writes all of this in one transaction. End the open assignment, insert the new assignment with reason ALLOCATION and the caller's service identity in created_by, and write EV-02 CaseAllocated to the outbox, plus EV-04 CaseTransferred when the case already had an owner. Add the unique index uk_assignment_open_case on assignment by case_id where ended_at is null and task_id is null, so a case holds one open case assignment. DecisionLogWriter.write runs last under Propagation.MANDATORY, so a failure throws, the whole transaction rolls back, the endpoint answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised under R-UNI-39.
RWB-E2-036.9: The controller answers the caller. Return 201 with the Assignment of the new owner. When every owner was at the cap, no owner is set, and the response carries the placement result with the overflow queue ID and no assignment, a response variant recorded in the additions file, so build both shapes of the reply. Two placements of one case committing at the same time leave one at 201 and refuse the other with 409 and MSG-GEN-004 through the optimistic lock on the case version, which AC11 tests. A placed case then shows on SCR-07 and SCR-02 like any other, and its entry on the decision log query SCR-38.

RWB-E1-004.1: Migration: creates the tables, columns and keys listed in section 11.
RWB-E1-004.2: Build: creates the entities, repositories, mapper/check/service classes listed in section 13.
RWB-E1-004.3: Build: registers the endpoint and published-interface contracts.
RWB-E1-004.4: Deferred: job scheduling, load execution and validation; see the data load reference.

RWB-E1-016.1: A person starts this. A user whose role may read the product opens the view for one case, and the front end calls GET /data-products/{productCode}/records with the product code and the case id. The product code is one of DP01 to DP14, and caseId is required: a call without it returns 400 with MSG-GEN-001. You build this path in DataProductController, with page and size for paging. The response is a DataProductRecordPage holding the record items, the product's freshness stamp, the page, the size and the total. Write a contract test for the endpoint from the additions schema recorded in RWB-TE-003.
RWB-E1-016.2: Automatic, and first in order. DataProductAccessService asks the ACE access check whether the caller's role holds right R in the capability area Case record. A capability right is the letter granted to a role for one area of the system, R meaning read here. The role codes come from the session, so your code queries neither the role table nor the permission table. A caller without that right gets 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no row is read. Keep this check ahead of the access row check and the scope call, in the order the build steps set out, so a caller who may read nothing never reaches the data.
RWB-E1-016.3: The same service then reads data_product_access through DataProductAccessRepository. A row in force is one whose role_code matches a role in the session and whose product_code matches the request, with can_read true, valid_from on or before today and valid_to not yet passed. No matching row gives 403 with MSG-P4-002, and the refusal goes to the access log with the user and the product. A row dated ahead of today does not count, as AC8 shows for RW-PHONECOL and DP06 valid from 2026-12-15 read on 2026-12-14. Create the table in this story's Flyway migration, a versioned SQL file the pipeline applies to each environment, unique on product_code, role_code and access_version.
RWB-E1-016.4: Automatic. DataProductAccessService calls CaseScopeQuery.linksInScope in P3 with the case id and the user context, and gets back a CaseLinks record holding the account ids and party ids of that case. When the case sits outside the caller's scope, P3 throws CaseNotInScopeException, the controller answers 404 with MSG-P4-003, the refusal is logged and no row is read. AC5 shows a case owner with scope Own asking for a case they do not own. Call the interface rather than reading P3 tables: scope belongs to P3, and this module never queries another module's tables.
RWB-E1-016.5: Automatic. Using only the account ids and party ids that P3 returned, DataProductRecordService reads the rows of the product's own entities from the P1 tables, among them party, contact_point, loan_account and collateral. Which entities belong to which product comes from sys_objects, so the service holds no product list in code. Build the read to return a record id, the entity and a map of field name to value, which is the shape the response items take. Apply the page and size from the request to the query, and leave every masking decision to the next step.
RWB-E1-016.6: Automatic. For every field read, DataProductRecordService finds the sys_fields row and checks is_personal. A personal field value goes through MaskingPolicy.apply from P4 with the object name, the field name, the value and the caller's role codes, and the returned text is what the response carries. When Compliance has loaded no masking rule, every personal field stays masked for every role, which is the behavior AC6 asks for with first_name, last_name, cif_no, date_of_birth and the contact value. Masking rule values are data owned by Compliance under RWB-E1-037, so write no rule into code.
RWB-E1-016.7: Automatic, and it happens before the response is returned. DataProductAccessService writes one entry through the ACE common module logging interface to PII Kafka, holding the user, the product code, the case, the names of the fields read and the time. No field value is ever logged. A refused call is logged the same way, with the user and the product. When the log write fails, the call is refused with 503 and MSG-GEN-006 naming the PII access log, and no personal field reaches the caller. Order the code to log first and answer second, which is build step 5.
RWB-E1-016.8: Automatic. DataProductController builds the DataProductRecordPage from the masked rows and adds the FreshnessStamp for that product, the same type RWB-E1-015 returns, so the reader sees which business date the values belong to. Fill page, size and total from the query. Map the failure paths to the responses in section 12: 400 for a missing caseId, 401 without a session, 403 with no capability right or no access row, 404 for a case out of scope, and 503 when the PII log or the store is down. Cover both new endpoints with contract tests from the additions schema.
RWB-E1-016.9: A person does this, and only a role holding right R in the capability area Platform administration, among them the data steward, Compliance, the center of excellence analyst, audit and the platform administrator. Build DataProductCatalogService to assemble one DataProductCatalogEntry per product from data_product, sys_objects, sys_fields and retention_rule, and return all 14 when no product filter is given. Each entry carries the product code and name, the definition, the owner role, the system of record, the refresh cycle, the expected-by time, the retention class and the field list with data type and the personal flag. AC2 expects the DP02 entry to list 20 fields with 9 marked personal.

RWB-E1-028.1: Automatic. Build TimerStarter as a listener on the three case events, which other stories publish when a case gets a queue and owner, moves to another owner, or changes status. Its first action is to stop the SERVICE_LEVEL timer the case is already running, setting that row to STOPPED so the old clock cannot warn or breach later. A SERVICE_LEVEL timer is the clock for one queue and status, so each new queue or status needs a fresh one. The partial unique index ux_timer_sl_running allows one RUNNING or PAUSED service level timer per case, which is why the stop comes before the start.
RWB-E1-028.2: Automatic, in the same listener. Call ProductParameterService.serviceLevel with the case's product group, its new status and the business date, which returns the limit, the unit, the warning percent and the escalation role. Then write a timer row with started_at at the event time, expires_at at the limit counted in working days by WorkingDayCalculator from the HOLIDAY table, and warn_at at the warning percent of that limit. AC1 places a hire purchase case in LIT-BKK-OFF at 2026-12-01 09:00 with a limit of 5 working days and 80 percent warning, giving expires_at 2026-12-09 09:00 and warn_at 2026-12-08 09:00, with 2026-12-05 to 2026-12-07 not working days.
RWB-E1-028.3: Automatic. Build PrescriptionService as a listener on CaseCreated. It reads case_account for the linked accounts, calls RecoveryDataQuery.accountDates in P1 for their contract and last payment dates, and reads the LEGAL_PERIOD row for the product through ReferenceDataService. For each account it adds the legal period to the last payment date, and where no payment exists it uses the contract date. The earliest of those dates goes to recovery_case.prescription_date. AC3 gives an account with last payment 2026-03-15 and a two year period, so the date is 2028-03-15. With no LEGAL_PERIOD row for the product, the date stays empty and the case is listed on the exception queue with MSG-P3-026.
RWB-E1-028.4: Automatic, in the same listener. Write a second timer row of type PRESCRIPTION with expires_at on the prescription date and warn_at that many days earlier, the number coming from the parameter legal.prescription.warn.days, which is 180. For the 2028-03-15 date of AC3 that gives warn_at 2027-09-17. Code the pause handler so it never touches this type: a deviation on the case leaves the prescription clock running with the same expires_at, because the legal period keeps passing whatever the bank does. GET /cases/{caseId} returns the prescription date on the Case schema for the screen to show.
RWB-E1-028.5: Quartz runs JOB-05 every five minutes under the service identity SY-CASEWF, with no person involved. Build TimerCheckJob to select timers with status RUNNING whose warn_at or expires_at is before now. Two partial indexes serve the two reads: ix_timer_due on expires_at and the new ix_timer_warn on warn_at, both limited to RUNNING rows, added in migration V028_1__timer_warn_index.sql. A partial index covers only the rows that match its condition, which keeps the query small as the table grows. PAUSED timers fall outside the status condition. The job has to handle the timers of 26,500 open cases inside one five minute cycle.
RWB-E1-028.6: Automatic. For each timer past its warn_at, the job writes a decision log entry and sends MSG-P3-003 to the case owner, naming the timer and its end date. The word once matters: add the column timer.warned_at, set it in the same write, and exclude rows that already carry it, so a later run does not warn again. AC11 has the warning sent in the run at 08:05 on Friday 2026-12-18 with end date Monday 2026-12-21, and no warning in the run at 07:55 the same morning, because the fourth working day had not yet passed.
RWB-E1-028.7: Automatic. Do the three writes in one transaction, which means the database keeps them together or discards them all: the decision log entry naming rule R-UNI-30, the timer row set to EXPIRED with escalation level 1, and the TimerBreached event in the outbox, the table events wait in until they are published, carrying the timer id, the case id and the escalation role from the service level row. When the decision log store is down the transaction does not complete, the timer stays RUNNING at escalation level 0, MSG-P7-003 goes on the job record, and the first run after the store returns raises the breach. Write no change to recovery_case: the queue and the owner stay as they are.
RWB-E1-028.8: Automatic. A timer of any type other than SERVICE_LEVEL, the PRESCRIPTION timer among them, takes the simpler path: set its status to EXPIRED and put a TimerDue event in the outbox with the timer id, the case id and the timer type. No escalation level is set and no escalation role is named, because only a service level breach goes to an escalation point. Keep the same guard as the breach branch, so a timer already EXPIRED is passed over and no second event is published for it when the job runs again.
RWB-E1-028.9: Automatic. Build TimerPauseHandler as a listener on the two deviation events. On DeviationRaised it sets the case's SERVICE_LEVEL timer to PAUSED, which takes it out of the job's selection. On DeviationCleared it sets the timer back to RUNNING and pushes expires_at and warn_at forward by the time the timer spent paused, counted in working days through WorkingDayCalculator. AC10 pauses from 2026-12-02 to 2026-12-04 and moves expires_at by two working days, while the PRESCRIPTION timer on the same case keeps running with its original expires_at.
RWB-E1-028.10: A person does this from SCR-03 Case record, which shows the prescription date and the due date of the running service level. Build GET /cases/{caseId}/timers in CaseAndWorkflowController to return a Timer array with id, caseId, timerType, startedAt, expiresAt, warnAt, paused, status and escalationLevel. Apply right R in the capability area Case record with the caller's scope, so a role without it gets 403 with MSG-P4-002 and a case out of scope gets 404 with MSG-P4-003. The prescription date comes back on the Case schema from GET /cases/{caseId}. Publish TimerService as well, for other modules that need the timers or the date.

RWB-E1-041.1: Automatic. JOB-12 already exists from RWB-E1-049 and runs every 15 minutes in business hours. Your change is to the job definition: put scanStep ahead of ocrStep, so no file is read for text until it has been checked for malware. The step runs under the service identity SY-OCR with Documents CRU rights, and no person starts it. With the feature flag rwb.dochub.malware-scan off, intake items are left unscanned, the OCR step does not read them, and an upload is refused with 503 and MSG-P5-022.
RWB-E1-041.2: Automatic. Write ScanStep to read document_intake rows whose scan_result is empty and pass each file to MalwareScanClient, the adapter to the bank malware scanning service. Each scan gets the timeout from the property rwb.dochub.scan.timeout-seconds, which is 30. The intake item ID is the key that makes the step safe to repeat: an item that already carries a scan result is not scanned again, so a rerun costs nothing and changes nothing. Build the client against a stub that flags the EICAR signature, the harmless test pattern scanners treat as infected, which AC1 uses in the file eicar-0002.pdf.
RWB-E1-041.3: Automatic, and the two outcomes part ways here. On CLEAN, set document_intake.scan_result to CLEAN and scanned_at to the time of the scan, which is what lets ocrStep pick the item up; scanned_at is a new column in your migration. On INFECTED, call QuarantineMover to move the file from the intake container to the quarantine container named by rwb.dochub.container.quarantine, set scan_result to INFECTED, write the audit event MALWARE_BLOCKED with the intake ID and the source, and alert the platform administrator. No document row is created for that file and the OCR step never reads it. Keep the file name and content out of the audit event.
RWB-E1-041.4: A person starts this one, by uploading a file in the dialog of SCR-30. The upload path built in RWB-E1-026 calls your published interface MalwareScanService.scanNow and waits for the answer before it calls DocumentStore.store. On INFECTED the caller gets 422 with MSG-P5-016 and the file is held in quarantine. When the scanning service does not answer, scanNow throws ScanUnavailableException, the caller gets 503 with MSG-P5-022, and neither a document row nor a blob is written. Your work here is the interface and the behavior behind it; the upload story makes the call.
RWB-E1-041.5: This behavior comes from RWB-E1-024 and already exists, so check it rather than build it again. When a clean file is stored, the document row takes the retention class and the write_once flag from the document type table, and a file whose type is marked write_once goes to the write-once container, where stored content cannot be changed afterward. AC2 expects a demand letter of type DEMAND_LETTER to carry class LEGAL10Y with write_once true and to sit in that container. The retention job later reads those two values and never alters a write-once blob.
RWB-E1-041.6: Automatic, on a Quartz schedule in Asia/Bangkok time, with no person starting it. Write RetentionJob to read every active document with its retention class, look the class up in the retention table version in force, and add period_months to the document's created_at date, which serves as the stored date. A document is due when that expiry date falls on or before the run date. AC3 has a GENERAL05Y document stored 1 November 2021, so 60 months gives 1 November 2026 and the run on 6 December 2026 finds it due. AC10 shows that an expiry date equal to the run date is also due. Work in committed chunks of 500 documents, so a stopped run resumes.
RWB-E1-041.7: Automatic. For each due document the job asks the P3 published interface CaseDirectory for the legal hold flag of that document's case, and when it is true the job does nothing to the document: no archive, no row on the review list. Add one to the held count that goes on the job record. A legal hold outranks the retention class for as long as it is in place, which is what AC5 checks on case RW-2026-000789. Read the flag through CaseDirectory rather than from the case table, because the case data belongs to another module.
RWB-E1-041.8: Automatic, and the end action of the class decides which path a document takes. For ARCHIVE, write the decision log entry with code DOCRET naming the document, its class, the table version and the expiry date, then move the blob to the archive tier and set the document state to ARCHIVED. Write the entry first: when that write fails the document is left as it is, MSG-P7-003 goes on the job log and the next run tries again. For REVIEW, add the document to the review list for Compliance and change neither the row nor the blob. The unique pair of document_id and run_month in retention_action keeps a document from being acted on twice in one month.
RWB-E1-041.9: Automatic. Build RetentionReviewWriter to write one CSV file per run at retention/review/{runDate}.csv, holding each listed document with its class and expiry date, together with any document whose class is missing from the version in force, marked as the exception RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING. AC4 names the file retention/review/2026-12-06.csv for the 6 December 2026 run. Write the five counts of due, archived, listed, held and exceptions to the job record, so the compliance and PDPA officer and the platform administrator read them on SCR-44. A rerun in the same month archives nothing again and leaves the listed rows as they were, which AC8 checks with 4 archived and 9 listed.

RWB-E1-053.1: Automatic. JOB-12 runs every 15 minutes in business hours and already holds the OCR and classification steps. Your change is to the job definition: add extractStep after classifyStep, so the document type is known, and before matchStep, so the extracted values are ready when the item is matched to its case. The step runs under the service identity SY-OCR with Documents CRU rights. With the feature flag rwb.dochub.extract off, extractStep sets extract_status to DONE with no fields, and items go on to matchStep with the OCR text only.
RWB-E1-053.2: Automatic. Write the selection query over document_intake for rows whose ocr_status is DONE and extract_status is PENDING, taking two groups: items classified with no review_reason, and items that already carry a document_id with a known type, which is the upload path. Select with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so a row another worker holds is passed over instead of waited for, which is how AC10 ends with one set of fields when two workers start together. The new index ix_intake_extract on extract_status for rows with ocr_status DONE serves this query. Add the three new intake columns in migration V1_5_053__extraction.sql.
RWB-E1-053.3: Automatic. For each item, read the field definitions of its document type from the DocumentTypeCatalog version in force on the business date, which is DOCTYPE-2026.11 with six types and 26 fields. Each definition carries the field name, the data type, the personal flag, the extraction method TEMPLATE or MODEL, the review_only flag and an optional pattern. Read EXTRACT_FIELD_THRESHOLD, EXTRACT_MAX_ATTEMPTS and EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS from document_hub_parameter in the same way. None of these values belongs in code, because the field list and the thresholds change through a load and an approval, not through a release.
RWB-E1-053.4: Automatic. Call OcrOutputReader from RWB-E1-049 for the text and layout of each page of the item, and pass what it returns to the extractor. Read it through that interface rather than querying the text table yourself. The layout matters for the template path, which finds a value by its position on the page and by the anchor text near it. Build your tests against fixed OCR pages, so the extractor behavior can be checked without running OCR, which is what the build steps ask for in TemplateFieldExtractor and ModelFieldExtractor.
RWB-E1-053.5: Automatic. Define FieldExtractor with one method that takes the pages, the field definitions and the timeout and returns a raw value and a confidence for each field. Write two implementations and choose between them by the extraction_method of each field definition: TemplateFieldExtractor for TEMPLATE, which works from layout and anchor text, and ModelFieldExtractor for MODEL, which calls the model through the P10 gateway with the text masked the way RWB-E1-050 masks it. Each result carries the extractor version, for example EXT-TPL-1.0 in AC1, so a later report can say which extractor produced a value.
RWB-E1-053.6: Automatic. Write ValueNormalizer to turn each raw value into the data type its definition names. Dates in Thai or English become ISO dates, a Buddhist Era year has BE_YEAR_OFFSET of 543 subtracted from it, Thai digits become Arabic digits, and amounts become numeric with two decimal places in baht. AC1 turns “1 ธันวาคม 2569” into 2026-12-01, and AC12 turns “3 October 2026” into 2026-10-03 and “THB 4,250,000” into 4250000.00. Unit test each conversion on its own, with the invalid date of AC6 among the cases, because this class carries most of the risk in the story.
RWB-E1-053.7: Automatic. For each field, FieldExtractionService sets the state from four conditions. A confidence at or above EXTRACT_FIELD_THRESHOLD gives OK, so the 0.8000 of AC5 passes at a threshold of 0.80 and the 0.6200 of AC3 does not. A value the normalizer cannot convert keeps its raw text with confidence 0.0000 and state REVIEW. A value that fails the pattern in its definition, such as the black case number format, also goes to REVIEW. A field marked review_only goes to REVIEW whatever its confidence, which AC4 shows with area_sq_wa at 0.9900.
RWB-E1-053.8: Automatic, and this is the path for an item not yet attached to a case. Write the fields as JSON into the new extracted_fields column and set extract_status to DONE. matchStep from RWB-E1-032 then passes those fields in the StoreRequest to DocumentStore.store, which writes one document_field row per field and sets document.review_status to PENDING when any field is in REVIEW. Your work with RWB-E1-024 is to check that StoreRequest carries the state, the extracted value and the extractor version, and that the store sets review_status. The case number and account number extracted here are what matchStep uses to find the case.
RWB-E1-053.9: Automatic, and this is the upload path, where the document already exists. Write the document_field rows yourself through DocumentFieldRepository, set document.review_status to PENDING when any field is in REVIEW, and put the DocumentFieldsExtracted event in the outbox, the table events wait in until they are published. All three happen in one transaction, so the rows and the event are applied together or not at all. The event payload carries the document id, the field names and the confidence, never a value. For a new version of a document, write new active rows and set is_active false on the earlier version's rows, which the unique index ux_document_field_active requires.
RWB-E1-053.10: A person does this. The case owner, or the litigation officer, opens SCR-30 for a case in their scope and sees each document with its fields, the confidence of each field and a mark on the fields in REVIEW. A document whose review_status is PENDING shows MSG-P5-003 with a link to SCR-31. Build the screen with a loading state of skeleton rows and a list state. The read applies right R in the capability area Documents with the caller's scope: a role without it gets 403 with MSG-P4-002, and a document outside the scope gets 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no field value, as AC13 shows for a case owner of team MTG-BKK reading a document of team HP-NE.

RWB-E1-065.1: The pipeline runs this, and a person only starts it by hand when they choose to. Add a DEV stage that fires on a merge to main touching any file under the recovery Flyway migration folder, and that a Tribe member or the platform administrator can also start manually. Flyway migrations are the versioned SQL files that build the schema, so a change to one is what makes the sandbox out of date. The stage is not a scheduled job and does not belong in the production job list. The pipeline holds a PostgreSQL advisory lock for the whole build, so a second build waits for the first to end, as the pipeline contract in section 12 states.
RWB-E1-065.2: Automatic. The stage builds the schema from the same migration files every other environment uses, so the sandbox cannot drift from the real schema. Point Flyway at the database rwb_sandbox and let it apply every recovery migration in order. That also creates sys_objects, sys_fields and the seed lists of values the generator reads in the next step, and it means no table is ever hand-built for the sandbox. A build that fails here leaves the previous sandbox in use, so the squads keep working while you fix the migration.
RWB-E1-065.3: Automatic. Build SandboxGenerator in tools/sandbox-generator, as its own build module that is never packaged into the ACE service. Before it writes anything it reads sys_objects for the tables, sys_fields for each column with its data type and personal flag, and lov_value for the allowed values of each list column, and works out the order to fill the tables from the relationships between them. Reading the dictionary this way is what lets a new column appear in the sandbox with no generator change, which AC3 checks by adding recovery_case.risk_tier. A column with no sys_fields row fails the build and names the table and column.
RWB-E1-065.4: Automatic. The generator writes 2,812 cases across the three product groups and the rows that hang off them in loan_account, party, contact_point, collateral, account_collateral, valuation, account_payment and interaction. A foreign key is the column that points at another table's row, and the generator fills tables in an order that lets every foreign key point at a row that exists, so a case has real accounts and parties to read. Every count comes from properties, among them rwb.sandbox.seed of 20261128 and the three case counts, so the same seed and commit give the same rows and the same totals, as AC5 checks.
RWB-E1-065.5: Automatic. Build ExceptionShapeBuilder to add ten cases for each shape BR4 lists: a duplicate case for one customer and product, a deceased customer, a bankruptcy, an open deviation, a legal hold, an unmapped product code, collateral with no account, a case with three accounts, accounts at 89 and at 90 days past due, and withdrawn consent. These are the shapes the rules have to handle, so a squad can test them from the first day without asking another team for data. The count is the property rwb.sandbox.shape-count. AC8 expects ten accounts at 89 days past due with no case and ten at 90 days past due with one open case each.
RWB-E1-065.6: Automatic. Build AccessSeedLoader to read the roles and permissions seed file and write the 54 roles, the role to permission rows and one named test user for each role. Every role gets a test user before it has real users, so a developer can call the DEV service as any role and see what that role may do. Those users are what the access tests use, among them the test user with RW-REFADM calling GET /cases and being refused with MSG-P4-002. Keep the rows in the seed file, so a permission change reaches the sandbox with no code change.
RWB-E1-065.7: Automatic, and it decides whether the build is published. Write SandboxVerifier with four checks: each table holds at least one row, each list column holds only values from its list in lov_value, each foreign key points at a row that exists, and no value matches a personal data pattern. The pattern check covers a 13 digit national ID with a valid check digit, a mobile number and an email address. Any failure fails the build with the table and column named, and the previous sandbox stays in use, which AC4, AC6 and AC7 expect. Nothing is published from a failed build.
RWB-E1-065.8: Automatic. Once the verifier has passed, the stage grants SELECT on the schema to the database role rwb_sandbox_read, which maps to the Entra ID group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE. SELECT on its own means a Tribe member can read and export rows and cannot change them, which is why AC2 expects an UPDATE by that role to be refused. The stage then publishes the build result with the row count of each table and the verifier outcome, so anyone can see what the current sandbox holds without querying it first.
RWB-E1-065.9: A person does this, and the point of the story is that they need no one else's help. A Tribe lead or squad member in the group runs SQL against the schema, writes a table to CSV with SandboxExport, or signs in to the DEV service as a test user and calls the normal endpoints, GET /cases among them. Build SandboxExport for the read-only role. The DEV profile points the service at rwb_sandbox under the feature flag rwb.dataengine.sandbox. The access rules still apply to those calls: a test user outside the case scope gets MSG-P4-003, and one without the right gets MSG-P4-002.

RWB-E2-009.1: Automatic. JOB-15 already exists from RWB-E1-013 and runs each night at 01:30 with no person involved. At the start of a run it reads the measure definitions in force from measure_definition through MeasureCatalog, which now include the seven steering measures of version MD-2026.12: CASES_BY_STAGE, CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE, DECISIONS_LOGGED, TREATMENTS, LETTERS_SENT, AGENT_ACCEPTANCE and AGENT_OVERRIDE. The reference data administrator loads that version and the Tribe lead approves it, so your code holds no measure list. Your change is to add the steering calculators and the reconciliation to the existing job.
RWB-E2-009.2: Automatic. Write SteeringCalculators with one calculator per measure code, each working on the previous business date. Take every figure through the published interface of the module that owns it: CaseReportingApi.caseFacts in P3 for cases by stage, queue and age, DecisionLogApi.decisionFacts in P7 for decisions logged, TreatmentApi.treatmentFacts in P3 for treatments, NoticeApi.noticeFacts in P6 for letters sent, and AgentMonitorApi.runFacts in P10 for the agent measures. Read no other module's tables. AC2 expects DECISIONS_LOGGED for 2026-12-15 to be 1,412, the count of decision log entries decided that day.
RWB-E2-009.3: Automatic. Build CountReconciliation to add up the CASES_BY_STAGE values it has just computed and compare that total with CaseReportingApi.openCaseCount for the same cut-off, which is the number the case list shows the teams. The tolerance is zero, so the two numbers either match or they do not. Write the comparison to the new measure_publish table with the business date, the dashboard count, the case list count and the status. AC2 has both counts at 240 and AC4 has 239 against 240. Run this before anything is published, which is the order build step 3 sets.
RWB-E2-009.4: Automatic, and the comparison decides the outcome. On a match, write the measure_snapshot rows for the business date with published_at set, and write the INT-19 extract for the data lake with its freshness stamp. On a mismatch, publish nothing for that date: measure_publish carries the held status and the reason, the previous day stays the latest published day, and an alert with MSG-P9-002 naming both counts and the date goes to the Reporting and BI analyst and the data steward. A held day is published by the first later run whose counts match, and a rerun of a published day writes the same values and leaves the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 alone.
RWB-E2-009.5: The refresh is scheduled in Power BI and the Reporting and BI analyst owns the report, so nothing in the Workbench triggers it. Your part is that the INT-19 extract for the business date is in place with its freshness stamp before 07:30, which AC1 states. Because Power BI and the screen read the same measure_snapshot rows, the committee and the teams work from one set of numbers. On a held day there is no new extract, so the report keeps showing the previous published day with that day's date.
RWB-E2-009.6: A person does this. Build SCR-37 as the React component SteeringDashboard, with filters for product, route and dates, a loading state of skeleton rows and a filtered state. It calls GET /reports/measures with those filters, which MeasureController serves from published measure_snapshot rows through MeasureQueryRepository. Dates in the wrong order are refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-003 naming from and to, as AC6 shows for from 2026-12-15 and to 2026-12-01. The Tribe lead, the product head, the team manager, the Reporting and BI analyst, the data steward and the Finance delegate are the roles that read this screen.
RWB-E2-009.7: Automatic. MeasureController checks right R in the capability area Reporting and applies the caller's scope, so a team manager sees only the teams in their scope and a role without the right gets 403 with MSG-P4-002. It returns published rows only, each with its period, and sets the response header X-Data-As-Of to the business date of the latest published day. Add the two new fields to the Measure schema in api.yaml and record them in the additions file: dimension, which carries the dimension code and value, and baselineValue, which carries the frozen 2026-11-27 figure the screen shows beside each value.
RWB-E2-009.8: Automatic, inside the same JOB-15 run. For each agent code and version, take the recommendations from AgentMonitorApi.runFacts and the verdicts from the decision log, then compute acceptance as accepted recommendations over all recommendations and override as overridden over all. AC3 gives agent case-intake version 1.2.0 with 200 recommendations, 170 accepted and 30 overridden, so acceptance is 85.0 percent and override is 15.0 percent. An agent with no recommendations that day has nothing in the denominator, so write no value for it and let SCR-37 show “No runs”, as AC7 expects for deviation-screen version 0.9.0. Carry the agent and version in the dimension, for example “agent:case-intake:1.2.0”.

RWB-E2-022.1: A person starts this. Build SendMessageDialog on SCR-03 for roles holding right C in the capability area Case record, with inputs for the channel SMS or LINE, the template, the language TH or EN defaulting to TH, and the party, which defaults to the borrower. The dialog posts to POST /cases/{caseId}/messages with an Idempotency-Key header. The channel and the template are both required: leaving either out is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 naming the field, as AC12 shows for a missing channel. The dialog also shows the refusal message when a check stops the send.
RWB-E2-022.2: Automatic. MessageController checks right C in the capability area Case record and applies the caller's scope, so a role without it gets 403 with MSG-P4-002 and a case outside the scope gets 404 with MSG-P4-003. MessageService then asks TemplateCatalog for the current Approved template for that code, channel and language. Only a current Approved template may be used, so a withdrawn template with no later approved version is refused with 409 and MSG-P6-003 naming the template, which AC6 checks with SMS-REMIND TH version 1. Templates are data from RWB-E1-046 and belong in no list inside the code.
RWB-E2-022.3: Automatic. Extend ConductCheckService from RWB-E2-021 with four tests that run before any message leaves the bank. It reads the legal hold flag of the case, asks DeviationApi.activeContactStops in S8 for open deviations with contact stop on, compares the open deviation codes against the reference list of codes that block the chosen channel, and calls PartyApi.contactPoints in P1 to confirm the party has a contact point of that channel that is verified and carries consent GIVEN. The blocking codes are reference data owned by the Conduct and QA officer, so the codes stay out of the code.
RWB-E2-022.4: Automatic. On a failed check nothing is sent. MessageService answers 409 with the message that fits the reason: MSG-P6-001 naming the deviation for a contact stop, MSG-P6-002 naming the channel when consent is missing, and MSG-P3-004 for a legal hold. It writes a decision log entry for the refusal and an interaction ledger entry with conduct check BLOCKED through InteractionLedgerApi.record, so the refusal is visible on the case. When the decision log store is down the refusal does not complete: the caller gets 503 with MSG-P7-003, nothing reaches NSS or LINE OA, and an incident is raised under R-UNI-39.
RWB-E2-022.5: Automatic. MessageService merges the case and party values into the template text, calls InteractionLedgerApi.record for an interaction with the channel, direction OUTBOUND, conduct check PASSED and delivery status Sent, and writes the send request to the outbox table of the ACE pattern. All three happen in one transaction, which means the database keeps them together or discards them all, so no message is queued without its ledger entry. The caller gets 202 with the interaction. Keep the phone number and LINE identifier as tokens in the request; the ACE notification path turns a token back into a real value.
RWB-E2-022.6: Automatic. JOB-11 runs every minute and picks up queued sends, with no person involved. Write MessageOutboxSender as its handler for message sends, calling NotificationPort.send with the channel, the contact point token, the template reference, the language and the case reference. The acknowledgment carries the reference NSS or LINE OA gave the message, which you write to the ledger entry as external_ref, for example NSS-7781 in AC1. The interaction ID is the idempotency key, so the same send is never dispatched twice. When the notification path is unavailable the send stays queued and is retried up to the limit of 5, after which it goes to the exception queue under R-UNI-34 and the entry becomes FAILED.
RWB-E2-022.7: The ACE notification path calls you here, so build MessageResultListener.onResult to take the external reference, the channel, the result and the time. Map the result to a delivery status through reference data: NSS result codes map to SENT, DELIVERED and FAILED, and LINE OA statuses map to DELIVERED and READ, both maps owned by the data steward. Then call InteractionLedgerApi.updateDelivery for that interaction. A LINE message reported delivered and then read ends at READ, which is what AC2 expects, and an NSS failure code ends at FAILED.
RWB-E2-022.8: Automatic. When a result maps to FAILED, call PartyApi.recordFailedContact in P1 with the contact point and the time, which raises that contact point's failed_count by one. AC8 has a contact point at failed count 0 before an NSS result of FAILED and at 1 after it. Make the call through the interface: contact_point belongs to P1, and this module writes none of its tables directly. The count is what later work uses to decide that a contact point is no longer reaching the customer.
RWB-E2-022.9: A person does this. The case owner, and a team manager, Conduct and QA officer or complaint officer holding right R in the capability area Case record, opens SCR-04 Case timeline and sees each message with its channel, the template used, the conduct check result and the current delivery status. The screen reads GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions, which P3 already serves, so no new read endpoint is needed. A blocked contact appears in the same list with conduct check BLOCKED, which is how the Conduct and QA officer sees what was stopped and why.

RWB-E2-028.1: Automatic. The case and workflow service identity SY-CASEWF creates the case and publishes CaseCreated, event EV-01, which already happens and needs no change from you. This story consumes that event: IntakeShadowListener from the earlier agent stories picks it up and decides whether to run the intake agent for the case. Nothing in this story creates or changes a case, and agent output never sets a case status, a task or a field. The case number used in the acceptance criteria, RW-2027-000501, is synthetic test data.
RWB-E2-028.2: Automatic, with no user waiting on it. Extend IntakeShadowListener to read the autonomy mode of the agent policy in force for the case's segment, which is L1 under policy INTAKE version P2, approved by RW-RISK from 2027-01-25. On L1 it runs the agent through the orchestrator, and the run is kept in agent_run with its agent code, version, mode, status, output, confidence, data_as_of and run time. The summary holds masking tokens only, so no personal value goes to the model or into the stored output. A segment whose mode is still SHADOW produces a run that is never shown to a user.
RWB-E2-028.3: A person does this. The case owner, holding RW-CASEOWN with Case record CRU, opens the case record for a case in their scope. SCR-03 already exists from RWB-E1-035 with its history timeline, and your change adds one panel to it. The screen has to load in under two seconds whether or not the panel has anything to show, so the panel loads beside the case record and never blocks it. In the read only state of SCR-03 the feedback controls are hidden.
RWB-E2-028.4: Automatic. Build GET /cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs to return an AgentOutput array read from stored agent runs, never by calling the model, so the case record waits for nothing. AgentOutputQueryService checks the caller's scope through the P3 interface and keeps only runs whose mode is L1 for the case segment, so shadow output never reaches a user and a case outside the scope gets 404 with MSG-P4-003. The response is an empty array when no L1 output exists, which is also what the endpoint returns with the feature flag rwb.agent.intake-l1 off. Right R in the capability area Case record is required.
RWB-E2-028.5: Automatic. Build AgentSummaryPanel as a React component on SCR-03 showing the summary text, each gap flag with its reason, the agent name INTAKE, the version INTAKE@P2/PR3 and the marker “Agent output”, so the reader always knows the text came from an agent and which version produced it. Add the three controls Accept, Correct and Reject. Build the panel states the story lists: loading with a skeleton, empty with no panel at all, unavailable with MSG-P10-005 when the run timed out or failed a guardrail, stale with MSG-P1-001 and the data date above the summary, ready, and recorded with the verdict and date and no controls.
RWB-E2-028.6: A person does this, and only a role holding right U in the capability area Case record, so a case owner may give feedback while a team manager reading a team case may not. The panel posts to POST /agent-runs/{runId}/feedback with the item key, which defaults to SUMMARY, the verdict ACCEPTED, CORRECTED or REJECTED, and an If-Match header carrying the run row version. A reason of up to 1,000 characters is required for CORRECTED and REJECTED: an empty reason is refused with 422 and MSG-P7-005 and nothing is stored. A correction records the reason and leaves the summary text alone.
RWB-E2-028.7: Automatic, and the order is the point of the step. AgentFeedbackService writes the decision log entry first through the P7 DecisionLogWriter, with the case id, decision code D6, the agent version INTAKE@P2/PR3, the model version, the agent run reference as the inputs reference, the recommendation holding the run id and the gaps, the final call as the verdict, the reason as the override reason and the owner as the approver. It then writes the agent_feedback row with the decision log id, both in one transaction, so the database keeps the entry and the row together or discards both. When the decision log write fails, the caller gets 503 with MSG-P7-003, no feedback row exists and the controls stay on the panel.
RWB-E2-028.8: Automatic. After a successful write the panel moves to its recorded state, showing the verdict and its date with the controls gone, and a second feedback request for the same run is refused with 409 and MSG-GEN-004, which the unique key on agent_run_id and item_key in migration V10_008__agent_feedback.sql enforces. JOB-15 then counts the stored verdicts into the rates SCR-46 shows by agent and segment. AC2 gives 300 feedback records for MORTGAGE and BKK in January 2027, with 240 accepted, 45 corrected and 15 rejected, so the acceptance rate is 0.8000 and the correction rate 0.1500.

RWB-E1-005.1: Migration: creates the tables, columns and keys listed in section 11.
RWB-E1-005.2: Build: creates the entities, repositories, mapper/check/service classes listed in section 13.
RWB-E1-005.3: Build: registers the endpoint and published-interface contracts.
RWB-E1-005.4: Deferred: job scheduling, load execution and validation; see the data load reference.

RWB-E1-017.1: A person starts this. Compliance owns the retention periods and prepares the rows; the reference data administrator submits them with POST /admin/reference-loads for table retention_rule, which needs the Reference data C right. A second person, the holder of Reference data A, then calls POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve. The reference data service from RWB-E1-043 already provides both endpoints, so your work is the handler behind the table name. Version RET-2026.11 is the first load, with one row for product DP05, table interaction, age basis occurred_at and 24 months. A version label that clashes with the one in force answers 409 with MSG-GEN-004.
RWB-E1-017.2: Your code does this with no person involved. RetentionRuleLoader.apply is the published interface the reference data service calls after approval, and it validates the whole load before storing anything. Check that product_code names a row in data_product, that table_name names an object in sys_objects, that the table is not decision_log_entry, that retention_months falls between 1 and 600, and that age_basis_field is a field of that table in sys_fields. A single bad row refuses the load in full with MSG-GEN-002 or MSG-P1-002, and RET-2026.11 keeps serving. The retention_rule table is new here, created by a Flyway migration, a numbered SQL file the pipeline applies to each environment.
RWB-E1-017.3: Nobody presses anything. Quartz is the scheduler inside the service, and it fires JOB-17 on the cron expression 0 30 2 ? * SUN#1 in the Asia/Bangkok zone, which is 02:30 on the first Sunday of each month. You write RetentionJob as the Quartz job class and annotate it with @DisallowConcurrentExecution so a second firing cannot overlap a run already going. A platform administrator can also start it from the job monitor with POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun; while a run is active that call answers 409 with MSG-P2-006. The trigger itself is already loaded before this story begins.
RWB-E1-017.4: RetentionService reads the rule rows itself at the start of the run. A rule is in force on the run date when its valid_from falls on or before that date and its valid_to is empty or later, so the version a run uses depends on when the run happens: a run on 2026-12-06 uses RET-2026.11, and a run on 2027-01-03 uses RET-2027.01 once that version starts on 2027-01-01. Keep the version label with the run, because an earlier run keeps the version it recorded even after a newer one takes over. Read the rows through RetentionRuleRepository.
RWB-E1-017.5: The job calls out to the case and workflow module for this, and the exclusion is absolute. CaseHoldQuery is a published interface of P3, so you never read recovery_case or its legal_hold column yourself. casesOnLegalHold() answers with the case IDs under hold, and every row of those cases is left in the live table whatever its age. In the test data, 40 interaction rows of case RW-2024-000311 are older than 24 months and all 40 are kept. Pair this call with caseNumbers() on the same interface, because the hold report in step 9 names cases by case number.
RWB-E1-017.6: The selection is pure code. For each rule, read rows of the named table and keep those whose age-basis field is older than the run date minus the retention months. The comparison is strictly older: with 24 months and a run date of 2026-12-06, a row with occurred_at of 2024-12-06T00:00+07:00 is kept, and only rows before that moment are selected. Drop the case IDs from step 5 before selecting. Work in batches of rwb.dataengine.retention.batch-size, which is 5000, and use the index ix_interaction_case_time over case_id and occurred_at. Nothing is deleted at this point.
RWB-E1-017.7: ArchiveWriter does this on its own, and it is the step that makes the deletion safe. Write the selected rows of each table as JSON lines files into the write-once archive container from RWB-TE-012, under the path retention/YYYY-MM-DD/<table>/ with the run date. Beside them write a manifest, a small file holding the row count and the SHA-256 hash of each data file. SHA-256 is a fixed-length fingerprint of the file content, so a file that was truncated or altered no longer matches. Read the manifest back from the container and compare both numbers before anything else happens. The container location comes from the property rwb.dataengine.retention.archive-container.
RWB-E1-017.8: Only after the manifest matches does the service remove the live rows, and the database refuses the delete unless you ask for it correctly. The interaction table carries an append-only trigger: a trigger is a function the database runs on every insert, update or delete, and this one refuses changes through refuse_change(). Your Flyway migration replaces that function so a DELETE on interaction passes when the transaction setting recovery.retention_purge is set to on. RetentionService sets it inside its own delete transaction and nowhere else. UPDATE is still refused, and decision_log_entry keeps the refusal with no exception. One transaction covers one table and one rule.
RWB-E1-017.9: The run writes its own record, with no person involved. On the JOB-17 job run, record the row count per data product and table, the rule version the run used, the archive location under retention/YYYY-MM-DD/, and the hold report. The hold report holds the case numbers from CaseHoldQuery.caseNumbers() with the number of rows kept for each, as with the single case holding 40 rows. Counts and case numbers only: no field value from an archived row goes into the run record, the log or a test. This is the content that GET /admin/jobs returns in the next step.
RWB-E1-017.10: A person reads the result; nothing in the flow pushes it to them. The Compliance officer calls GET /admin/jobs with the Platform administration R right and sees the JOB-17 run with its counts, rule version, archive location and hold report. The summary alert MSG-P1-020 carries the same figures in one line: the row count, the product, the rule and its version, and the number of cases kept on legal hold. Build that alert as part of this story. Reading the run is all the Compliance role may do here; a rerun needs the platform administrator, and RW-COMPLY posting one is refused with MSG-P4-002.

RWB-E1-029.1: A person does this in Excel. RW-COE fills the Rules template, which has a Rows tab for the rule rows and a Tests tab for the expected results. The rule table name and the version label are columns in the file, so ALLOCATION and ALLOC-2026.12 arrive inside the workbook rather than as separate parameters. Your work is RuleTemplateParser, which reads both tabs and keeps the spreadsheet row number of every row, because the refusal messages name rows by that number. Parse the 26 rows and 50 test cases of the example without changing their order; row order drives the overlap and unreachable checks later.
RWB-E1-029.2: The analyst uploads the file to POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions as multipart form data with three parts: the xlsx file, routeSet set to UNIVERSAL_RULES, and validFrom. The caller needs the Rules and parameters C right, so a role without it gets 403 with MSG-P4-002. The version label is the idempotency key, which means a second file carrying ALLOC-2026.12 answers 409 with MSG-GEN-004 rather than loading again. Two further refusals happen before any check runs: a valid-from date earlier than today answers 422 with MSG-GEN-003, and a template with no rows answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001.
RWB-E1-029.3: This runs automatically once the file parses. RuleLoadValidator is a published P3 interface and you write all four checks behind it. The schema check comes first: every required column present, each value of the right type, and list values matched against the P4 lists LOV-ASSIGN, LOV-ASSIGN-REASON, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-REGION and LOV-EXPOSURE. Then the overlap check, which refuses two rows that can both match one case at the same row order, because hit policy Unique allows only one condition to hold there. Then the unreachable row check, which refuses a row an earlier row already covers. Then the default row check for ALLOCATION. Each failure refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 naming the check and the rows.
RWB-E1-029.4: RuleTestRunner runs with no person watching. Take the 50 test cases from the Tests tab, evaluate each one against the draft rows, and compare the result with the expected queue or outcome in the file. Use the same evaluator the live engines use, so a passing test means the same answer in production. Any mismatch refuses the load with MSG-P3-027 naming the failing test case IDs, as with TA-07 and TA-19 expecting queue MTG-BKK-CO while the new rows answer MTG-CEN-CO. The minimum number of test cases is the parameter rules.testcases.min, which is 50, so read it rather than coding the number.
RWB-E1-029.5: RuleDryRun also runs by itself, and it changes nothing. Evaluate the draft rows against every open case and count the cases whose result would differ from the result the version in force gives, grouped by product and queue. Read the case fields through the P3 repository. The output is counts only, with no case numbers and no personal data, and it goes into the change log entry written in the next step so the approver can see the size of the change. This check refuses nothing on its own. Live cases have to be present for the counts to mean anything, which is why the story needs RWB-E1-018 in place.
RWB-E1-029.6: RuleVersionService decides the outcome with no person involved.
