Reading the case_party rows directly is not allowed; every cross-module read goes through the published interface. The result is the party IDs whose products the panel will show. Keep the role list in the property so the business can add a party role without a code change, and carry the party role on each item in the response so the screen can show whose product each line is.
RWB-E2-003.5: This happens on its own. Call CustomerProfileQuery.otherProducts(partyIds, excludeAccountIds) on the P1 published interface. The exclude set is the account IDs already on the case, read from case_account, so the case's own account never appears in the panel. The products come from party_product, a P1 table in data product DP02 that the COLLINS customer profile load fills through JOB-01 from UDP, SCBPDM and the core bank batch. Agree PartyProductView with the P1 squad first and build a stub to test against. A party with no other product gives an empty list, which the panel shows with MSG-P2-017.
RWB-E2-003.6: This happens on its own. Call DataProductStatus.freshness for DP02, which returns dataAsOf, expectedBusinessDate and a stale boolean. When the loaded date is older than the expected business date, set stale true on the response with messageCode MSG-P1-001, and log a stale read event holding the case ID and DP02. The products still go back to the caller, carrying the date they were loaded, so the case owner sees facts from yesterday and knows they are from yesterday. The panel then shows the banner naming the product Customer profile and that date.
RWB-E2-003.7: This happens on its own. For each item call Masking.apply on the ACE common module with the field party_product.account_no, the value and the caller's role codes. The masking rule rows are reference data owned by RW-COMPLY and loaded per DL26: clear for RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT, and masked to the last four digits for every other role with Case record R, so RW-PHONECOL sees XXXXXX5678 where a case owner sees 9900015678. Mask on the server, so the clear value never reaches the browser of a role that may not see it, and hold no masking logic of your own.
RWB-E2-003.8: This happens on its own, and it has to succeed. Call PiiAccessLog.write with the user, the case, the party IDs and the fields shown. When it throws PiiLogUnavailableException, return no products at all and answer 503 with MSG-GEN-006, because customer data is never returned without its access event. Write that path as a resilience test with a logging stub that refuses the event. The event holds case and party IDs only, never names or account numbers, and it is what lets the bank show under PDPA who read which customer record and when.
RWB-E2-003.9: This happens on its own in the browser. OtherProductsPanel renders one line per item with the product type, the account number exactly as the server returned it, the product status and the business date of the load. Status values come from the new list LOV-PRODUCT-STATUS, with values ACTIVE, DELINQUENT, CLOSED and WRITTEN_OFF; the P1 load check holds any unknown code, so the panel can show whatever code it is given. Show the stale banner with MSG-P1-001 when the response says stale, and the empty state with MSG-P2-017 when there are no items. The panel is read only and changes nothing on the case.

RWB-E2-015.1: A person does this, on the screen RWB-E1-035 already built. This story adds two panels to it, the React components CaseClocksPanel and DeviationPanel in src/modules/recovery/casewf/caserecord. The case owner has to hold Case record R and have the case in scope. Put both panels behind feature flag rwb.p3.case-clocks; with the flag off SCR-03 shows the Epic 1 read only fields and nothing else changes. Both panels are read only, so nothing the user does on this screen changes a timer, a deviation or the case.
RWB-E2-015.2: This happens on its own when the screen loads. Both endpoints exist in P3 already and this story extends them. GET /cases/{caseId} gains the array deviations, holding deviationCode, raisedAt, handlerUserId, approverUserId, pausedState, contactStop, clearedAt and outcome, plus the boolean deviationsAvailable. GET /cases/{caseId}/timers gains nextStepOwnerRole, escalatedToRole, escalatedAt, nextEscalationRole and inWarning on each Timer. Add the fields to the API file and regenerate the types the front end uses. Both need Case record R with scope applied, and both answer 404 with MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope. While the calls are in flight the panels show skeleton rows.
RWB-E2-015.3: This happens on its own on the server. Build TimerViewService with TimerRepository reading the timers of the case and, where timer.task_id is set, the owner_role of that task, which becomes nextStepOwnerRole so the screen can name who acts next. Show every timer with status Running, Paused or Expired, with its type, started_at, expires_at, warn_at, paused flag and escalation_level. Read through the existing indexes ix_timer_case_id and ix_task_case_id. Resolve the timer type labels through the P4 list interface from LOV-TIMER rather than writing them in code, and order the timers by due date for the panel.
RWB-E2-015.4: This happens on its own in CaseViewService, through two published interfaces. Call DeviationQuery.forCase(caseId) on the deviation module S8 with the 2 second timeout from caseview.deviation-timeout-ms, and for each deviation call DecisionLogQuery.approverOf(caseId, decisionCode, raisedAt) on P7, which returns the approver's user ID. Reading the deviation or decision log tables directly is not allowed. When S8 does not answer in time, set deviationsAvailable false and still return the case, so the timers and the on hold banner taken from recovery_case.deviation_open still show. The caller needs no Decision log right, because only the approver's user ID comes back.
RWB-E2-015.5: This happens on its own. Call ProductParameterService.serviceLevel(productGroup, caseStatus, businessDate) on the P3 interface from RWB-E1-045 and take the escalation role the SERVICE_LEVEL row names for that product group and status, for example RW-PRODHEAD for HIRE_PURCHASE at IN_PROGRESS. Return it as nextEscalationRole on the timer, beside escalatedToRole and escalatedAt. Those two columns are new: migration V<next>__rwb_e2_015_timer_escalation.sql adds timer.escalated_to_role and timer.escalated_at, and EscalationRecorder changes the escalation step of JOB-05 from RWB-E1-028 to write them. The escalation roles themselves are data rows set by the business.
RWB-E2-015.6: This happens on its own in the browser. CaseClocksPanel renders the timers from the response in due date order, nearest first. Per timer show the type label, the due date, the status, the escalation level, the role it was escalated to with the time, and the next escalation point. A paused timer shows the date it paused, for example Paused since 2026-12-10. Resolve role codes to display names through the ACE common module, so RW-TEAMMGR reads as Team manager. When the case has no timer with status Running, Paused or Expired, show MSG-P3-018 in place of the list. A breached service level changes neither the queue nor the case status.
RWB-E2-015.7: This happens on its own in the browser. Show recovery_case.prescription_date in the panel at all times, and add the warning MSG-P3-003 once the business date has reached the warn_at of the PRESCRIPTION timer. That warn_at comes from prescription.warning-days, which is 90, so a prescription date 60 days ahead warns and one 91 days ahead does not. Take the number of days from the configuration service rather than counting them in front end code. The prescription clock keeps running while a deviation is open, so this warning shows on a case on hold as well, which is the gap control CTL-18 was raised against.
RWB-E2-015.8: This happens on its own in the browser. While any deviation on the case is open, DeviationPanel puts SCR-03 in its On hold state with banner MSG-P3-004, which names the deviation and repeats the prescription date. List every deviation with its code label from LOV-DEVIATION, the handler, the approver from P7, the raised date, the return point, which is the routing state the case was in when it paused, and Contact stopped for codes X1, X2 and X3. A cleared deviation shows its cleared date and outcome. The case leaves On hold only once every open deviation is cleared, so with two open deviations the banner holds until both clear. When S8 did not answer, show MSG-GEN-006 naming Deviation handling in this section and keep the banner from the case flag.

RWB-E2-031.1: A person does this. The center of excellence analyst opens SCR-46 Agent monitor, which you build as the React component AgentMonitorPage in src/modules/recovery/agent/monitor, with filters for agent, segment and date range and a badge per agent and segment reading Shadow, live or paused. Build the common states as well: skeleton rows while loading, a sentence for a period with no runs, and an error message at the top. The menu entry shows only for a session holding Platform administration R. Put the page behind feature flag rwb.agent.monitor-v2; with the flag off SCR-46 shows runs and fallbacks only and the drift step is skipped.
RWB-E2-031.2: This happens on its own when the page loads. The access check refuses a session without right R in Platform administration with 403 and MSG-P4-002, as for RW-CASEOWN. Build the new endpoint GET /admin/agent-metrics with query parameters agent, segment such as MORTGAGE/BKK, from, to and version, and put its filter checks in AgentMetricsController: a from date later than the to date is 422 with MSG-GEN-003, and a range longer than 92 days is 422 with MSG-GEN-002 naming 1 and 92 days. The page asks for the last 30 days on first load. The endpoint is read only and applies the caller's scope.
RWB-E2-031.3: This happens on its own in AgentMetricsService. Build one AgentMetric row per agent, policy version, prompt version, model version, segment and date from three sources: the daily rows in agent_run_daily written by JOB-15, the agent_feedback verdicts, and the override counts from DecisionLogQuery.byAgentVersion on P7. Acceptance rate is accepted divided by accepted plus corrected plus rejected, so 119 accepted of 140 feedback entries gives 0.8500, and correction rate uses the same total. Override rate is the decisions on that agent version whose final_call differs from the recommendation, over all decisions on that version. Report latency as latencyP50Ms and latencyP95Ms. A segment is the case product group and region at run time, held on agent_run in the new columns segment_product_group and segment_region_code from migration V10_007__agent_run_segment.sql.
RWB-E2-031.4: The analyst drives this, and the screen calls the same endpoint again with the new filter values. The state badge comes from the autonomy mode of the agent policy for that segment, so one agent can be live on one segment and in shadow everywhere else, as SCREENING is for MORTGAGE and BKK. Shadow shows runs, fallbacks and evaluation scores and no acceptance, because nobody has given a verdict yet; live shows every measure; paused shows history only. A segment with fewer than 20 feedback entries in a week shows not enough feedback. From any row the analyst opens the runs behind it through GET /admin/agent-runs.
RWB-E2-031.5: This runs on its own on a timetable, with nobody watching. Add the step agentDrift to the nightly JOB-15 Reporting extract at 01:30, after the step agentRunDaily, and build it as DriftCheckStep. For each L1 agent and segment it reads the agent_feedback rows of the last 14 days and works out the acceptance rate of the last 7 days and of the 7 days before. The window of 7 days, the fall of 10 points and the minimum of 20 feedback entries per week all come from watch_measures on the agent policy, loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK, so none of the three sits in code. A segment under the minimum in either week is skipped.
RWB-E2-031.6: This happens on its own inside the same job step. When the later week's acceptance is at least 10 points below the earlier week's, insert one agent_alert row of type DRIFT holding the agent, the segment, the business date, measured_value, threshold_value, sent_to_role and sent_at; for 0.8600 falling to 0.7500 the measured value is 0.7500 and the threshold 0.7600. Send MSG-P10-006 through the P6 notification interface to the role named in agent_policy.alert_role and to RW-RISK. The unique key of agent_code, alert_type, segment and business_date means a rerun of JOB-15 for the same date writes no second row and sends nothing again.
RWB-E2-031.7: A person does this on the screen. Build OverrideReasonPanel to show, for one agent and one month, the count of decisions per coded override reason, taken from decision_log_entry.override_reason through the P7 query interface. An override is a decision where the person's final_call differs from the agent's recommendation, and REQ-APD-005 requires a coded reason on each one and a monthly report of them. Show counts only: no prompt text and no agent output content belongs on this screen. The same monthly view carries the token and cost reconciliation, showing not reconciled with the token difference when the daily rows and the run sums disagree.

RWB-E1-011.1: No person starts this. JOB-04 is a scheduled batch job, and you add a new step to it. A step is one unit of work inside a job, and Spring Batch runs the steps in the order the job defines. Build ReconciliationStepConfig in the package recovery.dataengine.recon and place it after the case list step and before the publish step. The step takes the business date from the job parameters, so every row it writes carries that one date. The job runs as the service identity SY-DATALOAD, so your step needs no user session. Add the checks REC-01 and REC-02 to the JOB-04 job mapping as well, so GET /admin/jobs reports them per product.
RWB-E1-011.2: The step makes this check itself; nobody confirms it by hand. Call LoadRunQuery, the published read interface from RWB-E1-003, with interface INT-01 and the business date, and read the status on the load_run row. Only the value COMPLETED lets the work go on. When the status is anything else, write no reconciliation_result row for that date, report every product as not run with MSG-P1-001 as the reason, and leave the case list publish held. This path is build step 5 in the solution plan. Reading another module's load table directly is not allowed, so the interface call is the only way to the status.
RWB-E1-011.3: ReconciliationService does this arithmetic once per product group, with no user involved. On the ALS side, count loan_account rows whose days_past_due is 90 or more, taking the 90 from the parameter case.entry.dpd rather than from code, then subtract the accounts that were excluded when cases were created. Those exclusion counts come from CaseQueryApi.excludedAccountsByProduct(businessDate), the P3 interface this story extends; do not query P3 tables for them. On the Workbench side, count case_list_row rows at the same days past due. Hold both numbers per product group, because each product gets its own result row and its own grade on the report.
RWB-E1-011.4: The same service method runs the second comparison automatically, inside the same step. Sum total_balance over the ALS accounts you selected for REC-01, and sum total_balance over the matching case_list_row rows, again per product group. Store the two sums as source_amount and workbench_amount, both numeric(18,2), so the money values keep two decimal places and nothing is rounded away. REC-02 uses the same product grouping and the same days past due filter as REC-01, so the two results for one product always describe the same set of accounts and a reader can compare them.
RWB-E1-011.5: The service computes variance_count and variance_pct, reads recon.tolerance.pct for that reconciliation from the parameter catalog, and sets result to PASS or BREAK. A variance above the tolerance is a break; a variance equal to the tolerance passes. Write the tolerance you used into tolerance_pct on the row, so a later reader sees which limit applied that day. Migration V1_011__reconciliation_result.sql creates the table with a unique constraint on rec_code, business_date and product_group. A unique constraint is a database rule that refuses a second row carrying the same three values, which is how two job runs on two nodes still leave six rows. ReconciliationResultRepository replaces all results for one date when the step runs again.
RWB-E1-011.6: The step writes these rows itself. Compare the two sets of account numbers in both directions and write one dq_exception row for every account that appears on one side only. Set check_code to REC-01, put the account number in record_key, set raised_on to the business date and status to OPEN. Nothing else about the customer belongs in the row. When a later run for the same date passes, set those rows to CLEARED with cleared_on, which is build step 3. Only a role with Platform administration R may list the rows through GET /admin/data-quality/exceptions; others receive 403 with MSG-P4-002.
RWB-E1-011.7: CaseListPublishGate makes this decision in code, with no approval by a person. Add publish_status to case_list_row with the values PENDING, HELD and RELEASED, and have the gate set HELD or RELEASED for the business date once all six results exist. Then change the publish step built in RWB-E1-002 so it writes the case list extract only when the status is RELEASED, which takes the place of the total count check that story used. On a break, LoadAlertNotifier from RWB-E1-003 sends MSG-P1-012 to the data steward, platform administrator and team manager groups, which are held as configuration. A held case list is never published by hand from here.
RWB-E1-011.8: ReconciliationExtractWriter produces both files inside the job run. Write reconciliation/<businessDate>.csv and data-quality/<businessDate>.csv and send them to the data lake through the outbound adapter INT-19. Add both writes to the publish step so the files travel the same path as the case list extract. A run for the same date writes the files for that date again, matching the results you replaced. These two files are the only input the Power BI report reads, so every column the report shows has to be in them. This is build step 6 in the solution plan.
RWB-E1-011.9: No code in the Workbench runs this. The reporting and BI analyst owns the report Reconciliation and data quality and its scheduled refresh at 07:30, which reads the two lake files from the previous step. Your work is to make those files carry what the report needs: one row per reconciliation and product with the counts, the balances, the variance and the result, the break rows with their account numbers, and the data quality failures by rule. The grades follow BR7: green when every reconciliation for the product passed, red when at least one broke, not run when the reconciliation did not run, with the reason. The story is done when the report shows the three grades from the SIT files.

RWB-E1-023.1: A person starts this. The case owner picks a case on SCR-02 Case list, and the front end opens SCR-03 Case record. Build the Loading state of SCR-03 as skeleton rows in each section, so the screen shows its shape while the five calls are still running. CaseRecordPage is the React component that owns this, in src/modules/recovery/casewf/caserecord. The whole screen is read only in Epic 1, so render no edit control anywhere on it. The feature flag rwb.p3.caserecordview controls the new page; with the flag off, SCR-03 shows the case header only.
RWB-E1-023.2: The page makes these calls on its own, and all five go out together instead of one after another, which is how the screen meets its two second target. Each section renders as soon as its own call answers. Give every call the limit held in the parameter caserecord.section.timeout.ms, which is 3000 milliseconds, and when one call fails or passes that limit, show MSG-P3-023 in that section and leave the other sections alone. Four of the five endpoints belong to P3 and the documents endpoint belongs to P5. Parallel loading with per-section messages is build step 4.
RWB-E1-023.3: The controller runs this check on every request, before any data is read. Two separate questions are asked. First, does the caller's role include the right Case record R; if not, answer 403 with MSG-P4-002. Second, is this case inside the caller's scope. Scope is the set of cases a role may open, and ScopeService from RWB-E1-037 gives it to you as a ScopeFilter: Own means the user's own cases, Team the team's cases, All every case. A case outside the scope answers 404 with MSG-P4-003 and shows no case data, so a user cannot learn that a case exists by asking for it.
RWB-E1-023.4: The service does this inside the request. Read recovery_case, case_account, case_party, interaction and queue from the P3 tables through CaseAndWorkflowRepository. For the account and party values, call RecoveryDataQuery.accountsFor and RecoveryDataQuery.partiesFor on the P1 interface with the IDs from the case links; querying P1 tables directly is not allowed. Each answer carries data_as_of, the date of the COLLINS load that produced it, and you keep that date beside each section rather than one date for the whole screen. Build step 1 covers this service and the per-section dates, with tests AC2 and AC3.
RWB-E1-023.5: MaskingApplier does both of these automatically on every read. Call mask(dto, session) from the P4 package built in RWB-E1-037, which hides the personal fields the caller's role may not see, so a customer number comes back with only its last digits visible. Then call AccessEventPublisher.publish with event code AC-READ, the field IDs that were read and a masked flag for each, which records who saw what. When that publish throws DecisionLogUnavailableException, mask every personal field and show MSG-P3-023 for Personal details; the rest of the case still shows. Personal fields are never shown unmasked when the access log write fails.
RWB-E1-023.6: This is another module's work, reached through GET /cases/{caseId}/documents, which P5 serves and which needs Documents R. You call it and render what comes back; you do not read document tables. Apply the same 3000 millisecond limit here as on the other sections. When the document hub does not answer in time, the Documents section shows MSG-P3-023 and the header, accounts, parties and contact history still show, which is what test TC-E1-023-06 checks. A case with no documents shows MSG-P3-024 instead, the sentence for a section that has nothing in it.
RWB-E1-023.7: The page renders this once the calls answer. CaseHeader shows the case number, product, status, stage, route, owner, queue, entry date, prescription date and the deviation and hold flags. Below it, AccountsPanel, PartiesPanel, ContactHistoryPanel and DocumentsPanel each show one section, and each carries a DataDateBadge with the business date of the data product behind it. Use the data_as_of value you kept per section in step 4, not the date the screen was opened. Fields appear as text with no edit control, because SCR-03 is read only until the editable view in Epic 2.
RWB-E1-023.8: The page decides this on its own, section by section. Compare each section's business date with the latest business date, and when the section is older, render StaleBanner above it with MSG-P1-001, which names the data product and its date. A refused COLLINS load is the usual cause, so the accounts section can be stale while the other sections are current, and each section is judged alone. The banner tells the case owner that the numbers below it come from an earlier day before they act on them. StaleBanner is build step 5, with test TC-E1-023-04.
RWB-E1-023.9: The page shows this automatically from the case it has already read. When the case status is ON_HOLD, render OnHoldBanner with MSG-P3-004, filling in the deviation or legal hold from deviation_open and legal_hold and the date from prescription_date. The prescription date is the date after which the debt can no longer be pursued, so the banner keeps it in front of the owner while the case is held. On hold is one of the SCR-03 states listed in section 15, beside Loading, read only, stale input and error, and each state has its own layout.

RWB-E1-035.1: A person does this. The case owner is already on SCR-03 Case record from RWB-E1-023 and chooses the Timeline panel, which this story adds. Build TimelinePanel in src/modules/recovery/casewf/caserecord/timeline and show skeleton rows while the call is running. The panel appears only when the feature flag rwb.p3.timeline is on; with the flag off, SCR-03 hides the panel and the endpoint answers 404. Nothing is fetched until the panel is selected, so opening the case record itself is not made slower by this story.
RWB-E1-035.2: The panel makes this call by itself when it opens. The endpoint is new work for you: api.yaml first lists it for Epic 2, and this story delivers it in Epic 1 behind the flag. Add page and size as query parameters. Paging means the server returns a slice of the events together with the total count, so a long history arrives in parts; page 0 with size 50 asks for the first fifty. The panel shows the total beside the items and asks for the next page when the user moves on. Paging with the total is build step 3.
RWB-E1-035.3: The controller runs this check on every call, with no person involved. A caller whose role does not include Case record R receives 403 with MSG-P4-002, which is what the access test does with RW-REFADM. A case outside the caller's scope receives 404 with MSG-P4-003, so RW-CASEOWN reads own cases, RW-TEAMMGR reads team cases, and RW-CONDUCT and RW-AUDIT read every case. Reuse the controller and the scope check that already serve the other case endpoints; this story adds one more method to them rather than a second check of its own.
RWB-E1-035.4: The service gathers from four places on each request. Read interaction and assignment through CaseAndWorkflowRepository, using the indexes ix_interaction_case_time and ix_assignment_case_id. Call DocumentQuery.documentsForCase for the documents and DecisionLogQuery.entriesForCase for the decision log entries; those tables belong to P5 and P7 and may not be queried directly. Give each outside call the limit in caserecord.section.timeout.ms, 3000 milliseconds. When the decision log does not answer, return the other three sources and MSG-P3-023 for Decisions, so a slow module costs one section only. This partial result is build step 4.
RWB-E1-035.5: TimelineItemMapper does this in code, with one mapper per source. The four sources hold different shapes of record, so each one becomes the same TimelineItem: at for the time, type for the kind of event, summary for one line of text built from code values and their labels, by for who or what caused it, and reference for the record it points back to. Keep personal data out of the summary and follow the masking rules by role for anything taken from a contact. Build step 1 covers the four mappers with their unit tests.
RWB-E1-035.6: The service sorts the merged list itself. Two events can carry the same timestamp, and a sort on time alone would then put them in any order, so two tie breaks follow. First the type order held in the parameter timeline.type.order: decision, status change, assignment, transfer, contact, document. Then the record ID, which settles two events of the same type at the same time. The result is the same on every opening, which AC5 checks with an assignment and a decision log entry both at 07:00:00. Return the slice the caller asked for together with the total count of events.
RWB-E1-035.7: The panel renders what the service returned. Give each type its own icon so a reader sees the kind of event without reading the text. For the by value, show the person when a person acted, and show the rule ID together with its version when a rule acted, taking rule_id and rule_version from the record. The version matters because rule rows change over time and the panel has to show which version was in force when the event happened. A new case whose only record is its creation entry shows one item with the entry rule and its version.
RWB-E1-035.8: A person opens the item, and the panel shows detail it already holds from the call. Build the detail view for a transfer: the transfer reason from transfer_reason_code with its label from LOV-TRANSFER-REASON, the owner and queue the case moved between, and the rule version. AC2 shows the shape with reason R04 Owner absent, the from owner, the to owner and rule version TRF-2026.11. The response fields reasonCode, fromQueueCode, toQueueCode and ruleId carry this detail. The panel and the item detail are build step 6, with test TC-E1-035-02 on a manual transfer.

RWB-E1-048.1: A person does this outside the Workbench. The center of excellence analyst opens a change request in the bank's own request tool and receives a reference such as CR-2026-0042. No code of yours creates that reference and no endpoint of yours calls that tool. What you build is the place to hold it: the column change_request_ref on reference_version, up to 30 characters, added by the migration in the solution plan. The reference ties a configuration change to the request that asked for it, and the approval check later refuses a version that carries no reference.
RWB-E1-048.2: A second person, the reference data administrator, uploads the version. Your work is to accept three more form fields on both existing load endpoints: changeRequestRef up to 30 characters, impactSummary up to 1000 and rollbackPlan up to 1000. A load with any of them missing still succeeds, because the fields are checked at approval and not at load. Pass the three values through to recordVersion on the published interface so they reach the version row. The two P4 load handlers are build step 2. Rule versions arrive by the same path, with a table code that starts RULE_ and names the route set.
RWB-E1-048.3: The service writes these values with no further action by a person. Store the three uploaded fields on the reference_version row, then set test_result to PASSED or FAILED. Where that result comes from depends on the table: for a reference table it is the outcome of the load checks built in RWB-E1-043, and for a rule table it is the outcome of the rule table test harness RWB-TE-005. The new columns all come from one migration: change_request_ref, impact_summary, test_result, rollback_plan, verified_by, verified_at and verify_note, with indexes for the period query of the report.
RWB-E1-048.4: A third person approves. The approver holds the approve right, which RW-RISK carries, and calls the approve endpoint that already exists from RWB-E1-043; this story adds checks to that endpoint rather than a new one. Until the approval happens, the version stays VALIDATED and is never served, even after its valid from date has passed, which is what AC2 shows with SERVICE_LEVEL version 5. The three people so far are different on purpose: one asks for the change, one loads it, one approves it, so no single person can put a new rule into force.
RWB-E1-048.5: The service enforces this inside the approve call, automatically. Build ChangeChecklistValidator and call it from approve. It refuses when the request reference, the impact summary or the rollback plan is empty, and when test_result is not PASSED, answering 409 with MSG-P3-022 naming the first item that is missing or failed. It also compares the caller with author_user_id on the version and refuses when they are the same person, with MSG-P7-002. A refused approval changes nothing: the version stays VALIDATED and the version already in force keeps being served.
RWB-E1-048.6: A person makes this call, and you build the endpoint. POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/verify takes a note of up to 1000 characters, which is required, and answers 200 with the load showing verifiedBy and verifiedAt. The caller needs Reference data U. Check the date against valid_from and answer 422 with MSG-GEN-003 when the verification comes too early, and 422 with MSG-GEN-001 when the note is empty. The call is idempotent, which means a second verification of the same version changes nothing and answers 200 with the first record, so a repeated click cannot overwrite who verified and when.
RWB-E1-048.7: A person reads the report, through a new endpoint you build. GET /admin/change-log takes from and to, both required, an optional table, format json or csv, and page and size with a default of 50 and a maximum of 200. It needs Rules and parameters R, so RW-AUDIT, RW-COE, RW-RISK and RW-PLATADM may read it and other roles receive 403. Answer 422 with MSG-GEN-003 when to is before from, and an empty list with total 0 for a period with no changes. ChangeEffectCalculator fills rowsAdded, rowsChanged and rowsRemoved by comparing a version's rows with the version it replaced by row_key and row_data, and lists the changed rule IDs for RULE_ tables. The report carries staff user IDs and no customer or case data.

RWB-E1-060.1: A person starts this. The center of excellence analyst uploads a CSV through the endpoint built in RWB-E1-058, one row per document and field: subject_type DOCUMENT, subject_id, label_key as the field name and expected_value as the value a person confirmed or corrected. The analyst needs Rules and parameters C. Each upload creates a new sample version rather than changing the one before it. Your work is SampleRowValidator, which checks every row against the P5 interface before anything is stored, and the hashing of personal label values with SHA-256 so the stored sample holds no readable customer data. A row naming a document P5 does not return refuses the whole file with 422 and MSG-P10-001.
RWB-E1-060.2: The analyst makes this call, with agent EXTRACT, sampleCode EXTRACT-S1, sampleVersion 1 and the three approaches OCR_TEMPLATE, MODEL and OCR_AND_MODEL. The endpoint answers 202 and the work goes on in the background, so the caller does not wait for the scoring. Write one agent_evaluation_run row with status RUNNING, the agent code and the sample code and version, and set it to DONE when the scoring finishes. Only one RUNNING run is allowed per agent and sample version, so a second request while the first is running receives 409 with MSG-P10-003.
RWB-E1-060.3: The run does this without a person and without the model. ExtractionApproachRunner calls DocumentQueryService.getFields(documentId) as SY-AGENT for each document in the sample and takes field_value and confidence as the P5 pipeline of RWB-E1-053 already wrote them. No prompt is sent and no token is spent, which is why a tie is later settled in this approach's favor. Do not read P5 tables; the interface is the only route to the fields. Keep the confidence of every field, because the threshold the story proposes later needs to know at which confidence the values were right.
RWB-E1-060.4: The run makes these calls itself, through AgentOrchestrator. Shadow mode means the model's answer is recorded and scored and never reaches a case or a document record, so a wrong answer here changes nothing in the Workbench. Use the approved policy EXTRACT version P1 with prompt PR1 and the allowed tools read_document_content and read_document_fields, and write one agent_run row per call with its status, latency, tokens and cost. When the model times out or fails a guardrail on a document, every labeled field of that document counts as a false negative for MODEL and the failure is counted on the evaluation run.
RWB-E1-060.5: The run does this as a third pass over the same documents. Send the stored OCR field values together with the document content to the same agent, and keep the values the model returns after it has seen both. This approach costs one model call per document, as MODEL does, so it sits between the two others when a tie has to be settled. All three approaches have to run over the same documents and the same labels, because the scores are compared with each other. Build step 3 adds this path and the MODEL path together, covering AC1 and AC4.
RWB-E1-060.6: FieldMatchScorer does the comparison in code. A value counts as a true positive when it equals the label after trimming spaces and folding case; dates are compared as dates, and personal fields are compared by their SHA-256 hashes. A wrong value is a false positive and a missing value is a false negative. Precision is true positives divided by true positives plus false positives. Recall is true positives divided by true positives plus false negatives. Write both to four decimal places on one agent_evaluation row per label_key and approach, with the sample size, and keep the model version and prompt version on the rows where the model was called.
RWB-E1-060.7: ExtractionProposalBuilder computes this and writes it to the proposal column on the evaluation run; no person chooses at this point. F1 combines precision and recall as two times precision times recall divided by their sum. Take the approach with the highest mean F1 across the type's fields, and settle a tie in favor of fewer model calls, OCR_TEMPLATE before OCR_AND_MODEL before MODEL. The proposed threshold is the lowest confidence at which every chosen field reaches the target precision of 0.95, and a field that never reaches it is proposed as review-only. A type with fewer labeled documents than the minimum of 30 is scored and marked insufficient sample, with no approach and no threshold proposed. The target, the minimum and the tie order sit on the policy row.
RWB-E1-060.8: Two people act here and neither part is automated. The analyst reads the scores and the proposal through GET /admin/agent-evaluations, which needs Rules and parameters R, and exports the proposal rows by asking for text/csv. The solution architect then writes the architecture decision after ADR-009, which happens outside the code and is out of scope for this story. Nothing the evaluation produced changes how documents are handled today: a proposed threshold takes effect only when P5 loads it as a new reference data version. Your work ends at the CSV export, which is part of build step 5.

RWB-E2-004.1: A service makes this call, with no user involved. The ACE plan status reader from RWB-E2-002 runs under the service identity SY-CASEWF, and in SIT a test harness calls the same method. Build the published interface TreatmentRecords in the S2 package recovery.treatment.record.api together with the command it takes: case ID, treatment type, who proposed the plan and when, offer and haircut amounts, installments, valid until, approval level, the decision log entry ID of the approval, the first due date and an idempotency key. That key is a value the caller sends so a repeated call is recognized and not handled twice. The approval happened before this call, so what you record is a plan that is already approved.
RWB-E2-004.2: The service runs both checks automatically before it writes anything. Ask the P3 case interface whether the case exists and what its status is, and refuse a closed case with MSG-P3-005. Ask the P7 interface for the decision log entry named in the command and read approver_user_id on it; refuse with MSG-GEN-001 when the entry is unknown or carries no approver. The decision log holds who decided what, and these two checks keep a plan from being recorded without a traceable approval behind it. S2 reaches the case only through the P3 interface, never through P3 tables.
RWB-E2-004.3: TreatmentRecordService does this in code. Check the required fields, that installments are above zero for a restructure, that the first due date is on or after the proposed date, and that the treatment type is a value in LOV-TREATMENT. Then write the treatment row and the outbox row for TreatmentApproved inside one transaction. A transaction is a single database unit of work that either saves everything in it or saves nothing. The outbox is a table the event is written to so it is sent only after the commit. Together they keep any event from naming a treatment that was not saved, and any treatment from being saved without its event. The migration creates treatment with first_due_date and its two indexes.
RWB-E2-004.4: The listener reacts to the event on its own, after the write of step 3 has committed. Build PlanTimerListener in recovery.casewf.plan. It reads the case route state, which is the position of the case inside its route and is held apart from the case status, and it looks for the first due date in the event terms. Only a case in BOOKED_IN_ALS_NLEADS carrying a first due date counts as SCHEDULE_SET and goes on to the rule. Keep the event ID, so a repeated delivery is ignored and counted; test TC-E2-004-08 sends the same event twice and expects one timer and one decision log entry.
RWB-E2-004.5: The rules component SY-RULES answers this call, and logic of this kind does not belong in your listener. Pass the case and the event to it and take back the action, the to state PLAN_RUNNING and the version of the rule row that matched. The rule rows R-RES-25 and R-RES-27 sit in the Restructure route set and are loaded by the center of excellence through RWB-E1-029, so a condition can change without a code change. Hold the returned rule version, because the next step writes it to the decision log entry and to rule_version on the case. When no rule matches, the case goes to the exception queue with MSG-P3-005.
RWB-E2-004.6: The listener does this in a fixed order you have to keep. Write the decision log entry through the P7 interface first, with rule R-RES-25 and its version. Only when that write has succeeded may you create the INSTALLMENT_DUE timer, set route_state to PLAN_RUNNING and publish CaseStateChanged with the from state, the to state, the rule ID and the decision log entry ID. When the decision log store is unavailable, no timer and no state change happen, the event is retried three times and then goes to the exception queue with MSG-P7-003. PlanTimerService sets the timer to expire at the first due date, 23:59 Asia/Bangkok, and sets warn at plan.warn-days earlier. The unique index on treatment_id, timer_type and expires_at stops a second timer for the same due date.
RWB-E2-004.7: JOB-05 is the timer job from RWB-E1-028. It runs every five minutes and needs no change of its own. When it finds a timer past its expiry it publishes TimerDue and moves the timer status from RUNNING to EXPIRED. Your part is to make the INSTALLMENT_DUE timers it reads carry what the event needs, including the treatment_id column this story adds to timer with the index ix_timer_treatment_id. Test TC-E2-004-02 moves a controlled clock past 2026-12-31 23:59 and expects the event and the EXPIRED status, so the timer has to be readable by the job without further work.
RWB-E2-004.8: Another module does this. P8 payment matching in JOB-07 decides that an installment went unpaid and publishes PaymentMissed with the treatment ID, the due date and the amount due. Building that matching is out of scope here, so you work against the event contract and a test that publishes the event by hand. Nothing in this story reads payments or judges whether money arrived. What you need from the payload is the treatment ID and the due date, because the next step uses them to find the plan and start its cure period.
RWB-E2-004.9: The same listener handles the second event automatically. Call the rules component for R-RES-27, write the decision log entry with that rule and its version first, and only then create the CURE_PERIOD timer and set route_state to PLAN_CURE_PERIOD. The cure period is the time the customer has to pay a missed installment before the plan counts as broken, and its length is CURE_PERIOD_DAYS, a product parameter read through ProductParameterService; for MORTGAGE it is 30 calendar days. Handling a plan that is still unpaid after the cure period belongs to a later epic. This path is build step 6, with test TC-E2-004-12.
RWB-E2-004.10: This runs each night at 01:30 with no person involved. Add TreatmentExtractStep as a Spring Batch step in JOB-15. It calls TreatmentRecords.changedSince for the business date, so P1 reads treatments only through that method and never from the S2 table, and writes one row per treatment to the DP04 treatment data product. Derive each row's status: APPROVED while booked at is empty, BOOKED once it is set, and RUNNING, BROKEN, COMPLETED or CANCELED from the outcome. The business date is the idempotency key, so a second run replaces that date's extract instead of adding a copy. A failed run leaves the previous date in place, shown with MSG-P1-001.

RWB-E2-016.1: A person navigates here. SCR-04 is a new screen in this story, opened from the case record, and it holds the full timeline with its filters and the queue history. The timeline panel inside SCR-03 from RWB-E1-035 stays as it is. Build CaseTimelinePage in src/modules/recovery/casewf/timeline with a Loading state of skeleton rows and a Filtered state for the list after a filter is applied. The feature flag rwb.p3.full-timeline controls the new screen; with the flag off, the user sees the older panel on SCR-03.
RWB-E2-016.2: The page makes the call on its own when it opens, and again each time a filter changes. The endpoint already exists from RWB-E1-035, and this story adds page with a default of 0, size with a default of 50 and limits of 1 to 200, the type and date filters, and unavailableSources in the answer. Keep the chosen filters in session storage, so a user who leaves the screen and comes back sees the same view. Answer 422 with MSG-GEN-002 when size falls outside 1 to 200. The new parameters are build step 3.
RWB-E2-016.3: TimelineService runs this check on every call. First the case: a caller without Case record R receives 403 with MSG-P4-002, and a case outside the caller's scope receives 404 with MSG-P4-003. Then the item types: Decision log R allows decision items, Documents R allows document items, Litigation R allows notice items. A caller without one of those rights simply sees no items of that type, with no error, which is what a phone collector sees on the AC5 case. Run the rights check before the source calls, so you never fetch what the caller may not read.
RWB-E2-016.4: The service does all of this inside one request. Read assignment, interaction and timer from the P3 tables through AssignmentHistoryRepository and InteractionRepository, using ix_assignment_case_id, ix_interaction_case_time and ix_timer_case_id. At the same time call DecisionLogQuery.forCase, DocumentQuery.forCase and NoticeQuery.forCase, each on its own thread so the three waits overlap instead of adding up. The limit is the parameter timeline.source-timeout-ms, 2000 milliseconds. A source that does not answer in time is left out, its name goes into unavailableSources, and the screen shows MSG-GEN-006 naming it while the items from the other sources still show.
RWB-E2-016.5: TimelineItemMapper and the service do this in code. The seven kinds of record have different shapes, so each becomes the same timeline item: the time, the type, a one line summary built from code values and their labels, the actor and a reference to the record behind it. Mask personal data in a contact summary by role through the ACE common module, and never log it. Merge the lists into one, order them newest first, keep the order of each source's own sequence for items that share a time, and return the page the caller asked for with the total count.
RWB-E2-016.6: The page handles its own states. Show skeleton rows while the call is running, then the list of items with type, actor and time. When the user changes the type filter or the date range, call the endpoint again and show the answer in the Filtered state. Type labels and reason code labels come from LOV-ASSIGN-REASON and LOV-TRANSFER-REASON through the P4 list interface, so no wording sits in the code. A filter that matches nothing shows MSG-P3-019, and a date range with to before from is refused with MSG-GEN-003 naming the two fields.
RWB-E2-016.7: A person opens this view, and it reuses the same endpoint. QueueHistoryTab asks for types ASSIGNMENT and TRANSFER only, and renders one row per move with the queue and the owner the case came from and went to, the reason code with its label, and the rule ID. The queue on the assignment comes from RWB-E2-012, so an assignment written before that story has no queue_id and its row shows Queue not recorded. The first allocation of the case is one of these rows and shows with reason ALLOCATION, which test TC-E2-016-03 checks together with the three transfers.
RWB-E2-016.8: A person opens the item, and the front end then calls the P7 endpoint with the entry ID that the timeline item already carries as its reference. That call needs Decision log R, which the caller holds, because an item of this type reaches only a caller with that right. A decision log entry is never changed after it is written, and a correction appears as a further entry, so the page shows what was decided at the time. Keep no copy of the entry in P3 tables; the timeline holds the reference and reads the entry through P7.

RWB-E2-032.1: A person starts this. The restructuring officer opens the treatment record screen SCR-14 for a restructure treatment created by RWB-E2-004, in its draft state. Your work on the screen is TreatmentSuggestionPanel, a new area in the draft state that shows either the suggestion with its model code and version, or MSG-P10-007 when no suggestion is available. The officer goes on editing the offer fields as before; the suggestion is never copied into them and never changes the treatment status. The feature flag rwb.agent.tdr-suggestion controls the whole path and, when off, makes suggestOffer answer empty with no call.
RWB-E2-032.2: The treatment service makes this call when the screen opens, with no separate action by the officer. Build the published interface ModelSuggestionClient in recovery.agent.api with one method, suggestOffer, which returns an optional suggestion and can throw DecisionNotRecordedException. An empty answer is a normal outcome and means the screen shows MSG-P10-007. The call runs as SY-CASEWF. The treatment type is checked before any model work: a treatment of type SETTLEMENT gets no model call and no suggestion, because the model is called only for type RESTRUCTURE.
RWB-E2-032.3: TdrSuggestionService does this first, automatically. Read the policy row TDR_OFFER that is in force and look at autonomy_mode. Mode OFF means the model is not in service: answer empty at once, make no gateway call and write no decision log entry. That is the state the story ships in, because policy version P1 has mode OFF with review date 2027-02-28 until the TDR team deploys the model. When they do, RW-COE loads a new version with mode L1, the model code and version, the output schema and the 60 second timeout, and RW-RISK approves it. GET /admin/agent-configs shows which version, mode and review date are in force.
RWB-E2-032.4: TdrInputAssembler gathers the inputs in code. Read principal outstanding, total balance, days past due and the interest rate for the account, and the payment dates and amounts of the last twelve months, all through the P3 interface; those tables belong to another module and are not queried here. Mask the personal fields, the account number among them, before anything leaves the service, so the model request carries no identifying customer data. Hold the masked set as a snapshot, because the decision log entry written later points to it as the inputs reference.
RWB-E2-032.5: The service makes the call through ModelGatewayClient from RWB-E1-058, which is the only route to the model and uses the private endpoint of integration INT-23. Use the timeout from the policy row, 60 seconds. Then check the answer against the output schema tdr-offer-v1, which allows installments from 1 to 360, a monthly amount above zero, an interest rate from 0 to 30 and a confidence. A timeout writes the agent run with status TIMED_OUT and fallback true; an answer that fails the schema writes GUARDRAIL_FAILED with check SCHEMA. In both cases no suggestion is returned, the screen shows MSG-P10-007, and the officer carries on with the treatment.
RWB-E2-032.6: The service writes both records before it answers. The decision log entry goes through the P7 DecisionLogWriter with decision code D5, the model version, the inputs reference, the suggested terms as the recommendation, final call SUGGESTION_RECORDED, and the treatment ID and agent run ID in its actions. The agent run row holds the status, the model version, the latency, the guardrail result, the output and the decision log entry ID. When the decision log write fails, return no suggestion, throw DecisionNotRecordedException so the treatment service can show MSG-P7-003, keep the run row without a decision link and raise an incident.
RWB-E2-032.7: The service answers the call it received in step 2, returning an OfferSuggestion with the agent run ID, the decision log entry ID, the model code and version, the installments, the monthly amount, the interest rate and the confidence. A suggestion is returned only after its decision log entry has been written. The answer is idempotent under the key TDR_OFFER plus the treatment ID, which means a second request for the same treatment returns the first suggestion and the same decision log entry ID and makes no second model call. Publish EV-28 AgentRunCompleted for the run.
RWB-E2-032.8: A person reads the panel and decides. TreatmentSuggestionPanel shows the suggested terms together with a line naming the agent and the model version, as AC3 shows with Suggested by TDR_OFFER, version TDR-OFFER-1.0. The officer types the offer fields and submits the offer, because the suggestion is advice and nothing applies it. Roles with Treatment and offer R, among them RW-RESTRUCT and RW-CASEOWN, may read it. Reading the agent runs through GET /admin/agent-runs needs Platform administration R, so RW-RESTRUCT is refused there with MSG-P4-002.

RWB-E1-012.1: Migration: creates the tables, columns and keys listed in section 11.
RWB-E1-012.2: Build: creates the entities, repositories, mapper/check/service classes listed in section 13.
RWB-E1-012.3: Build: registers the endpoint and published-interface contracts.
RWB-E1-012.4: Deferred: job scheduling, load execution and validation; see the data load reference.

RWB-E1-024.1: The caller is another part of the Workbench, either the upload service from RWB-E1-026 acting for a person who holds Documents C, or the OCR intake from RWB-E1-032 running under the service identity SY-OCR. You build the entry point they call: the published interface DocumentStore in package recovery.dochub.store, with a store method taking caseId, documentType, source, intakeBlobRef, sha256, fields and partyId. A published interface is the only way another module may reach this code, so no caller writes the document tables for itself. The file sits in the intake container at this point, and the hash is the SHA-256 the caller computed over the file content, which step 5 uses to find a repeat.
RWB-E1-024.2: DocumentStoreService runs this check with no person involved. Call CaseDirectory.findById, the P3 published interface from RWB-E1-018, and refuse the store when it returns nothing. The guardrails forbid reading another module's tables, so never query recovery_case from this package even though the case ID is in hand. BR1 makes document.case_id mandatory, which is why the case has to exist before anything is written. The fields you keep from the case are its id and case_no. Build this check first in DocumentStoreService.store, together with the type, content and size checks of the next two steps, so that a refusal happens before the transaction opens.
RWB-E1-024.3: The service reads this by itself through DocumentTypeReader, which you build over the document type table that RWB-E1-025 created. The version in force is the one whose valid_from and valid_to dates cover today, DOCTYPE-2026.11 at release. Take write_once and retention_class from that row and copy them onto the document. BR3 says the caller never supplies either value, so ignore anything a caller sends for them. A type that is not in the version in force is refused with 422 and MSG-P5-006, and nothing is stored. Unit test the version in force on a boundary date, where one version ends and the next begins.
RWB-E1-024.4: The service does this, again before the transaction opens. Read the file's own leading bytes, its content signature, and accept the file only when those bytes say PDF, JPG or PNG. A Word file renamed to .pdf therefore fails, which is test TC-E1-024-06. A file outside the allowed list is refused with 415 and MSG-P5-001, and a file above the limit with 413 and MSG-P5-017, which shows 25 MB. Both values come from document_hub_parameter, read through DocumentHubParameters and cached for five minutes. This story creates that table in migration V1_5_024__document_store.sql with a unique key on param_code and table_version. AC7 fixes the boundary at 26,214,400 bytes.
RWB-E1-024.5: The service decides this alone. Query for an active document row with the same case_id, document_type and content_sha256, and when one is found return it and write nothing more: no second row, no decision log entry, no event. This behavior is called idempotent, meaning the same call made twice leaves the same single result. Back the check with the unique partial index uk_document_case_type_hash on document (case_id, document_type, content_sha256) where is_active, which the migration creates, so that two calls arriving together still produce one row. Test that the index refuses a second active row with the same three values.
RWB-E1-024.6: The service performs all four writes, and a transaction means they commit together or none of them commits. Call DecisionLogWriter from RWB-E1-027 first, with decision code DOCATT and final call STORED; it writes inside your transaction. Then insert the document row with doc_version 1 and state COPY_PENDING, insert one document_field row per extracted field, and put the DocumentStored event (EV-16) into the outbox, a table the publisher reads after commit so that an event cannot be sent for a store that rolled back. A failed decision log write leaves no row and no event, which gives MSG-P7-003 and is test TC-E1-024-14. Write an integration test that forces the writer to fail.
RWB-E1-024.7: The service continues on its own after the commit. Call DocumentStorage.store from RWB-TE-012, which writes the blob and refuses an overwrite; never write to blob storage any other way. Pass container rwb-docs-legal when the type row has write_once true and rwb-docs when it is false, with the path {container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1. On success set storage_ref and move the state from COPY_PENDING to STORED. When the container refuses the write the row stays COPY_PENDING, content reads return 503 with MSG-GEN-006, and CopyPendingStep, the step you add to JOB-12 Document intake, retries the copy on the next run. Container names are properties per environment.
RWB-E1-024.8: A person who holds Documents R does this from SCR-30 Case documents, which RWB-E1-026 builds. You add DocumentDetailPanel, the React component that opens from a row of that screen, and the two read endpoints behind it. GET /documents/{documentId} returns the metadata, the extracted fields and the version list; GET /api/recovery/v1/documents/{documentId}/content returns the file of that version as application/octet-stream. Both apply the right R in Documents and the caller's scope, so a case outside the scope returns 403 with MSG-P4-003 and no metadata or content. A write-once document shows no edit control and the label Write once. The ACE common module writes the PII access log entry for each read, so your package writes none.
RWB-E1-024.9: A person who holds Documents U does this, through POST /documents/{documentId}/versions with multipart form data: the file and a reason, which is required. Build addVersion in DocumentStoreService. Insert a new document row with doc_version n+1 and previous_version_id pointing at the current row, then set is_active false on that earlier row, which stays readable through the content endpoint. Only the latest version takes a new version, so a call on an inactive row is refused with 409 and MSG-P5-025. The optimistic lock column version on DocumentEntity gives the second of two parallel calls 409 with MSG-GEN-004, leaving exactly one new row. The migration adds previous_version_id with a foreign key to document(id), a column whose value has to match an existing row's id.

RWB-E1-037.1: A person starts this. The reference data administrator, holding RW-REFADM and the right C in Reference data, builds the matrix file from the approved workbook, puts the application owner's approval reference in the file header, and posts it to POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/reference-loads as multipart form data with the file, table set to permission and a validFrom date. The endpoint already exists from RWB-E1-043; your work is the handling behind it for the permission and masking_rule tables, through AccessAndAdministrationController. The approval that the file header names happens outside the Workbench, so your code carries the reference and never checks it. A repeat with the same Idempotency-Key header returns the first response.
RWB-E1-037.2: The Workbench does this with no person involved. Build PermissionMatrixLoader to check the whole file before it keeps any part of it: every active role appears exactly once for each of the 14 capability areas, the letters come from C, R, U, D, A in that order or the single character -, and every role code is known. A file with any error is refused in full with MSG-P1-002, which names the failed check, and the version in force stays untouched. A file that passes is stored as rows in the permission table with status Loaded and the new matrix_version. Add the unique index uk_permission_version on permission (matrix_version, role_id, capability_area) so that one role and area cannot be stored twice for a version.
RWB-E1-037.3: A second person acts here. The security administrator, holding RW-SECADM, reads the difference report against the version in force and calls POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve. Build that difference report in the loader so that the approver can see which letters changed before deciding. The request has no body. Nothing of the loaded version takes effect until this call succeeds, which is why the work is split across two roles: RW-REFADM may load and may never approve, and RW-SECADM approves for the permission table. A repeat approve of a version already approved returns 409 and writes nothing.
RWB-E1-037.4: ReferenceLoadApprovalService does all of this in one transaction, meaning the checks, the decision log entry and the status change commit together or none of them commits. Read the approver role for the table from the parameter catalog: rwb.refload.approver.permission names RW-SECADM and rwb.refload.approver.masking_rule names RW-COMPLY. A caller without that role is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002. The person who loaded the version may never approve it, which returns MSG-P7-002 and leaves the version Loaded. Then write one decision log entry through the P7 writer with decision code AC-VERS and no case, and set the version to Approved with its valid from date. A failed decision log write leaves the version Loaded and returns 503 with MSG-P7-003.
RWB-E1-037.5: This happens on its own, with no deployment and nobody pressing anything. From the valid from date, each new session reads the approved version when it resolves the caller's rights, so the screens and endpoints that the new letters open start working. Sessions already open keep the version they resolved at sign-in, which RWB-E1-022 handles. Your work is to make the lookup of the version in force a query by date instead of a value in code, so that AC1 passes: a user holding RW-LEGAL gets 403 from GET /queues under PM-2026.11 and 200 under PM-2026.12, with the same build deployed.
RWB-E1-037.6: A person makes the request, and two parts of the Workbench share the work. Build ScopeService as a published interface with scopeFor(SessionContext), returning a ScopeFilter that carries the type OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL, the user reference, the team codes and the region codes. The type comes from role.default_scope, and the teams and regions come from the P3 queue membership interface of RWB-E1-019. The owning module then puts that filter into its own query, because this package may not read another module's tables. OWN covers cases the person owns or has a task on, TEAM the cases in their team queues, REGION the cases in the regions of their teams, and ALL every case. Scope filters first, and the permission check follows.
RWB-E1-037.7: The Workbench does this, through the AccessCheck of RWB-E1-022 that runs on every endpoint. The check reads the letters that the matrix version in force gives the session's roles for the capability area the endpoint belongs to, and refuses the call with 403 and MSG-P4-002 before the handler runs. A capability area holding - refuses every action in it. The refusal is written as an event with the area and the right that was missing, for example area QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION and right U when a case owner calls the transfer endpoint. The check itself needs no new code; confirm it through the AccessCheckInterceptor on that endpoint, and make sure the records reaching it are already limited to the scope from step 6.
RWB-E1-037.8: The Workbench does this, in code you build as the published interface FieldMasker. Mark every personal field on a DTO with the annotation @PersonalData carrying its field ID, which covers the party identity number, the date of birth and the contact point value. FieldMasker then replaces each value unless a row in the masking version in force gives one of the session's roles unmasked true for that field. A field with no row is masked, so a session makes no request for a clear value it may not see. Where a rule does allow it, fetch the clear value through the ACE PII service, which logs the read to PII Kafka as INT-22. Masking runs before data reaches a screen or an agent. The number of characters kept comes from rwb.access.mask.keep-last, set to 4.
RWB-E1-037.9: The Workbench does this on every request, in SessionRevalidationFilter. Compare the group memberships held on the session with the memberships the ACE common module currently holds for that person, refreshed at most every five minutes under rwb.access.membership-refresh-minutes. When a group that gave the person a role has gone, end the session and refuse the request with 401 and MSG-P4-001, and refuse a new sign-in as well. Removal from the Entra ID group is the work of the bank access administrator and is started by the line manager, both outside the Workbench, so your code only reacts to the change. Test it with a group removed in the ACE test double during an open session.

RWB-E1-049.1: This runs on a schedule with nobody starting it. JOB-12 Document intake fires from its Quartz schedule every 15 minutes during business hours in Asia/Bangkok. You build DocumentIntakeJob as a Spring Batch job with ordered steps, and add ocrStep as the step that runs after the intake and scan steps. The order matters because BR3 lets a file be read only once its malware scan says CLEAN, and that scan step arrives in RWB-E1-041; until then test data is seeded with scan_result CLEAN. A stopped run leaves its unfinished items PENDING for the next run, and the platform administrator can also rerun the job from the job monitor through POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun.
RWB-E1-049.2: The Workbench does this by itself, as soon as a document is stored. Build DocumentStoredListener to consume the DocumentStored event (EV-16) that RWB-E1-024 publishes, keep only the events whose source is UPLOAD, and insert one document_intake row for each: the case ID, the document ID and scan_result CLEAN, because an upload is scanned before it is stored. ocr_status starts at PENDING from the column default and ocr_attempts at 0. This row is the unit of work for the rest of the flow, and its ID is the idempotency key of the OCR step: an item whose status is no longer PENDING is never read again.
RWB-E1-049.3: The step does this with no person involved. Select document_intake rows with scan_result CLEAN and ocr_status PENDING, oldest first by received_at, using SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. That clause takes a lock on each row it returns and passes over rows another worker already holds, so two workers never take the same item and the second simply moves on. Index ix_intake_ocr_pending on (ocr_status, received_at) where scan_result = 'CLEAN' serves the query. Run up to OCR_WORKERS items at a time, four at release, through a worker pool. Test this with one pending item and four workers starting together: the OCR service has to receive exactly one call.
RWB-E1-049.4: Your adapter does this, under the service identity SY-OCR. Build OcrClient with a read method taking the blob reference, the list of languages and a timeout, and OcrServiceAdapter behind it calling the OCR service that Autonomous Ops runs, at the endpoint in the property rwb.dochub.ocr.endpoint. Send Thai and English together, because a Thai recovery document often carries English words as well. The answer gives, for each page, the lines, the words, their positions, the language and a confidence value per word. Map a call that does not answer within OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, 120 at release, or that returns an error, to OcrUnavailableException, and a file that cannot be opened to UnreadableFileException. Build this against a stub returning fixed pages first.
RWB-E1-049.5: The step does this on its own for each item. Take the mean of the word confidence values on a page as that page's quality. Write the whole OCR answer as JSON to the standard container at ocr/{intakeId}.json and put that location in document_intake.ocr_ref. Keeping the full output lets classification in RWB-E1-050 and extraction in RWB-E1-053 read the lines and positions without a second call to the OCR service, which they do through the published interface OcrOutputReader that you build in this story. The guardrails keep OCR text out of application logs, so log the intake ID and the counts only.
RWB-E1-049.6: The step writes these rows itself. Insert one document_text row for each page: intake_id, page_no, text_content and quality, and document_id as well when the intake item is already attached to a document, which it is for an uploaded file. Migration V1_5_049__document_intake.sql creates the table, with a foreign key from intake_id to document_intake(id) and from document_id to document(id); a foreign key means the value has to match an existing row in the other table. The unique key uk_document_text_page on (intake_id, page_no) stops a second set of rows for the same item, so a repeat run cannot double the text. Test that index first.
RWB-E1-049.7: The step decides the status with no human step. Compare every page's quality with OCR_MIN_QUALITY, 0.70 at release. When every page is at or above it, set ocr_status DONE; the threshold counts as a pass, so a page at exactly 0.70 is accepted. When any page falls below it, set ocr_status RESCAN and put the page numbers of the failing pages in rescan_pages. A four page document with page 3 at 0.41 therefore gives status RESCAN and rescan_pages 3. The threshold is a parameter row in document_hub_parameter, loaded by the reference data administrator, so a change to it needs no release.
RWB-E1-049.8: The step does this for each item it set to RESCAN, and the branch depends on whether the item has a case. With a case ID, RescanNotifier sends MSG-P5-018 to the case owner through the ACE notification path, naming the page, the document and the case; the owner comes through CaseDirectory, never by reading the case tables. Build RescanNotifier and add the message template to the ACE notification path under the recovery templates. With no case, send nothing and set review_reason RESCAN, which puts the item on SCR-31 Document review queue once RWB-E1-054 is built. A mailroom scan with no case therefore gets no notification.
RWB-E1-049.9: The step does this at the end of its run. Count the items read, the items set DONE, the items set RESCAN and the items that failed, and write those four counts onto the JOB-12 job record. The platform administrator reads them on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor, which shows a run as running, failed or complete, and reruns the job from there when needed. The same record carries the step failure that AC6 expects: two runs in which the OCR service answered 503 show the OCR step failed in both, and the job raises an alert to the platform administrator after the second. The counts hold no document content.

RWB-E1-061.1: A person starts this. The center of excellence analyst calls GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report for the evaluation run that RWB-E1-059 finished, and sets Accept to application/json, text/csv or application/pdf for the format wanted. You add the endpoint to AgentEvaluationController. The right needed is R in Rules and parameters, which RW-COE, RW-RISK and RW-AUDIT hold; a case owner is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002, which is test TC-E1-061-08. The call is read only, and the same run always gives the same report. A run that has not finished is refused with 409 and MSG-P10-008.
RWB-E1-061.2: The Workbench builds this with no person involved, in EvaluationReportService. Read the stored rows of agent_evaluation_run, agent_evaluation and agent_run, and put together the sample size, the agreement rate for each gap type, the count of each failure type, the total cost and the cost per case, the median and 95th percentile latency, and the policy, prompt and model versions. Cost per case is the total cost divided by the number of runs to four decimal places, so 412.6000 baht over 200 runs gives 2.0630. Latency percentiles count every run, with a timed out run counted at 60,000 ms. The report holds counts and rates only, and no personal field. Build it over a fixture of 200 runs.
RWB-E1-061.3: The analyst does this, and you build what makes it possible. EvaluationReportExporter writes both the CSV and the PDF from the same report object that step 2 built, so the three formats cannot disagree with one another. The format is chosen by the Accept header on the report endpoint, with no second endpoint. The analyst then puts the export into the pack for the steering committee, which is work outside the Workbench; the committee meeting and its minutes are out of scope. Keep the export clear of personal fields, as the report itself is.
RWB-E1-061.4: The analyst does this. RW-COE posts the new policy version to POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-configs with kind POLICY and agent INTAKE, carrying autonomy mode L1, the ID of the evaluation run it rests on, the conditions, the fallback and the measures to watch. The endpoint comes from RWB-E1-058; this story adds the L1 checks behind it. The right needed is C in Rules and parameters. The four new values are stored on agent_policy by migration V10_004__policy_promotion.sql, which adds evaluation_run_id as uuid, promotion_conditions and watch_measures as jsonb, and fallback_rule as varchar(20). The fallback of an L1 agent is the rule result.
RWB-E1-061.5: The Workbench checks the proposal with no person involved, in PromotionProposalValidator, which you add inside AgentConfigService and run only for mode L1. Three checks apply. The named evaluation run has to have status DONE. Its sample size has to be at least 200, the minimum held in the policy JSON schema version the loader uses. Every condition stated in the proposal is compared with the scores of that run, and a score below a stated condition refuses the load while naming the gap type and the value. The conditions, the fallback and the measures to watch all have to be present. A failed check refuses the whole file with 422 and MSG-P10-001 and leaves the version in force unchanged. A file that passes is stored with status LOADED.
RWB-E1-061.6: A second person does this. The risk and model risk officer, holding the right A in Rules and parameters, calls POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve with a valid from date once the steering committee has agreed. Reuse the approval check from RWB-E1-058 and test it for an L1 version. The person who loaded the version may never approve it, which returns 409 with MSG-P7-002. Until this approval succeeds and the valid from date arrives, version P1 in SHADOW mode stays in force, so no agent output reaches case owners on the strength of the proposal alone.

RWB-E2-005.1: A person does this on the screen you build. DecisionLogQueryScreen is SCR-38 Decision log query, a React component with fields for one case or a list of cases, the decision, the rule ID, the rule version, the approver, and a from and to date. Build its Loading, Results, Export and Empty states. The filters caseIds, holding up to 500 case IDs separated by commas, and ruleVersion are new in this story and are recorded in the additions file. The internal auditor holds the right R in Decision log with scope ALL, so the screen is open to them for every case; a role whose Decision log letter is - never reaches it.
RWB-E2-005.2: The screen does this, with no further action from the auditor. It calls GET /decision-log with the filters the auditor set, plus page and size. The endpoint exists as API-P7-006; this story adds the caseIds and ruleVersion parameters, the chainVerified field on each item, and text/csv as an Accept value for the export. Add the parameters to the API specification as well as to DecisionCenterAndLogController. The response is a DecisionLogPage carrying items, page, size and total, with the warning MSG-P7-012 at the top when any entry on the page fails its check. Size runs from 1 to 500 under the parameter rwb.decision.query.max-size.
RWB-E2-005.3: The Workbench does this in DecisionLogQueryService. Validate the filters first and refuse a bad one with 422: a from date later than the to date gives MSG-GEN-003 naming the field, and a size or case count outside its limit gives MSG-GEN-002 with its minimum and maximum. Then apply the caller's scope, which you get from ScopeService.scopeFor in P4 and pass to the P3 interface casesInScope(ScopeFilter, Collection<UUID>); only entries whose case comes back are read, and the number of entries left out is never shown. Run the query in chain_seq order, the sequence number each entry carries in the log. Add index ix_declog_approver_time on (approver_user_id, decided_at) in migration V_E2_005__declog_approver_index.sql.
RWB-E2-005.4: The Workbench does this for every entry it is about to return, in ResultChainCheck. Recompute entry_hash from the entry's canonical form, the fixed layout that RWB-E1-008 defines for hashing an entry, and compare the stored prev_hash with the hash of the entry before it in chain_seq order. The pair of checks is what shows a change: a changed field gives a different entry_hash, and a removed entry breaks the link. Set chainVerified true or false on each item from the result. The entry before the first one on the page sits outside the page, so read one extra row per page to check it. The query path writes nothing to any entry.
